# EDI API key

## Why a key

Since **2026-07-30** the EDI repository's PASTA+ REST API requires authentication for
every request, including reads of public data[^edi-news-20260727]. An anonymous request
is refused with HTTP 403 ("Public Access … not authorized"), or 401 from the audit
service. Keys are free.

edi-mcp is a hybrid: with a key it talks to PASTA; without one it reads the anonymous
DataONE replicas of EDI content (see [Backends](../tools/backends.md)). A key gives you
the authoritative, up-to-date repository and, once they are built, the operations only
PASTA offers. The server carries a short version of this page as the
`edi://guide/api-key` resource[^api-key-guide].

## Create a key

1. Sign in at [auth.edirepository.org](https://auth.edirepository.org/auth/ui/signin){target=_blank}[^edi-auth]
   with Google, Microsoft, GitHub or ORCID. A free EDI profile is created on first
   sign-in.
2. Open **Access Keys** from the avatar menu at the top right, or go straight to
   [auth.edirepository.org/auth/ui/key](https://auth.edirepository.org/auth/ui/key){target=_blank}.
3. Choose **New Key**, give it a name (for example `edi-mcp`), and set **Principal** to
   your own profile. A group principal limits the key to that group's access.
4. Copy the key.

EDI's own guide: [Working with access keys](https://edirepository.org/resources/working-with-access-keys){target=_blank}[^edi-access-keys].

## Give it to edi-mcp

- **stdio (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, …):** set `EDI_API_KEY` in the server's
  environment, for example
  `claude mcp add edi -s user -e EDI_API_KEY="$EDI_API_KEY" -- edi-mcp --transport stdio`
  ([Clients](clients.md) has every client). `EDI_MCP_EDI__API_KEY`, when set, takes
  precedence.
- **HTTP deployments:** each caller sends their own key in the `X-EDI-Key` header. It is
  honoured only when the server's `public_base_url` is `https://`. The operator's key is
  not lent to callers unless `share_config_key_over_http` is enabled, and the MCP
  `Authorization` header is never forwarded to EDI. See
  [Hosted HTTP deployment](../deploy/hosted-http.md).

There is deliberately **no command-line flag** for the key: arguments show up in `ps`
output and shell history. edi-mcp does not load `.env` files itself, and it ignores
look-alike names such as `EDI_KEY`, `EDI_TOKEN` and `EDI_AUTH_TOKEN` (it logs a warning
when one of them is set without `EDI_API_KEY`).

edi-mcp exchanges the key for a short-lived `edi-token` (8 hours) at
`auth.edirepository.org`, keeps it in memory only, renews it before it expires, and
sends it to PASTA as a cookie. If the authentication service is unavailable it falls
back to passing the key as a query parameter to PASTA. The key and the token go only to
EDI hosts and never appear in results, logs or errors; every URL edi-mcp reports is
scrubbed first.

## Check the key

`edi-mcp --check` only reports whether a key is configured (`keyConfigured`) and which
backend that selects; it makes no network request. To confirm that EDI accepts the key,
ask your agent to call `edi_ping` with `check_api=true`. The `api` block of the result
shows `reachable: true` and `credential: "token"` (or `"key"` when the query-parameter
fallback was used). A refused key shows up as an `error` with code
`upstream_forbidden`.

## Without a key

Without a key, edi-mcp answers from DataONE. The tools available today all work that
way; several planned tools will need a key. Entity listings carry a keyless
`anonymousUrl` (a DataONE member node) beside PASTA's `dataUrl`.

| Operation | Without a key (DataONE) | With a key (PASTA) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Search (`edi_search_packages`) | yes | yes |
| Scope list (`edi_list_scopes`) | dated snapshot | live |
| Identifiers and revisions (`edi_list_identifiers`, `edi_list_revisions`) | yes | yes |
| Package overview, metadata and data entities (`edi_get_package`, `edi_get_metadata`, `edi_list_entities`) | yes | yes |
| Data preview and download *(planned)* | yes | yes |
| Citations *(planned; cite.edirepository.org)* | yes | yes |
| Quality reports, lineage, change feeds, read counts *(planned)* | no | yes |
| Whole-package zip download *(planned)* | no | yes |

See the [Roadmap](../tools/roadmap.md) for the planned tools.

Caveats of the fallback: the DataONE index can lag new EDI uploads by a day or more and
may not hold every scope or revision PASTA has; the DataONE member nodes proxy PASTA, so
EDI could restrict them too. `source.backend` in every result says which backend
answered.

## Errors

- `auth_required`: the operation needs a key and none is configured for this call. The
  error points at the `edi://guide/api-key` resource.
- `upstream_forbidden`: a key was sent and EDI refused the request.
    - Without a `reason` (HTTP 401): EDI rejected the key (mistyped, expired, deleted, or
      a group key without access). Fix or replace the key.
    - With `reason: access_restricted` (HTTP 403): the key works, but this package is
      restricted to named users or groups. A new key will not help; ask the package's
      contact for access or pick another package.

edi-mcp never silently falls back to DataONE in either case: a bad key is an error, not
a downgrade.

[^edi-news-20260727]: EDI news, 2026-07-27. <https://edirepository.org/news/news-20260727.00>

# Clients

Local clients start edi-mcp themselves over **stdio**; hosted deployments are reached
over **Streamable HTTP**. The [install script](install.md#option-1-from-source-with-the-install-script-recommended)
(`scripts/install.sh`) writes the stdio entries below for Claude Code, Claude Desktop,
Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Goose and OpenCode in one step; this page shows them for manual
setup. The examples use `edi-mcp` on your `PATH` (see
[Install](install.md)); replace it with an absolute path such as
`/home/me/edi-mcp/.venv/bin/edi-mcp` when the client does not share your shell's
`PATH`. JSON-configured clients do not expand `~` or `$HOME`, so use absolute paths
there.

The key is optional; [EDI API key](api-key.md) shows how to create one. Every example
passes it as `EDI_API_KEY`, the name EDI's own guides use. Put it in the client's
environment settings, never in a shared or committed file. Leave it out and edi-mcp
uses the anonymous DataONE backend.

## Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add edi -s user -e EDI_API_KEY="$EDI_API_KEY" -- edi-mcp --transport stdio
claude mcp list
```

`-s user` makes the server available in every project[^claude-code-mcp]; drop the `-e`
option to run without a key.

## Claude Desktop

Edit `claude_desktop_config.json` and restart the app:

- macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
- Windows: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`
- Linux: `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "edi": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/edi-mcp",
      "args": ["--transport", "stdio"],
      "env": { "EDI_API_KEY": "paste-your-key-here" }
    }
  }
}
```

## Codex CLI

```bash
codex mcp add edi --env EDI_API_KEY="$EDI_API_KEY" -- edi-mcp --transport stdio
codex mcp list
```

This writes the server into `~/.codex/config.toml`[^codex-mcp]; restart running
sessions.

Without the CLI, add the table to `~/.codex/config.toml` yourself:

```toml
[mcp_servers.edi]
command = "/absolute/path/to/edi-mcp"
args = []

[mcp_servers.edi.env]
EDI_API_KEY = "paste-your-key-here"
```

## Gemini CLI

```bash
gemini mcp add --scope user -e EDI_API_KEY="$EDI_API_KEY" edi edi-mcp
gemini mcp list
```

or add the entry to `~/.gemini/settings.json`[^gemini-mcp] (`.gemini/settings.json` in a
project):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "edi": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/edi-mcp",
      "args": [],
      "env": { "EDI_API_KEY": "paste-your-key-here" }
    }
  }
}
```

## Goose

Add an extension to `~/.config/goose/config.yaml` (Windows:
`%APPDATA%\Block\goose\config\config.yaml`)[^goose-ext], then restart Goose Desktop or
start a new CLI session. `goose configure` → *Add Extension* → *Command-line Extension*
does the same interactively.

```yaml
extensions:
  edi:
    enabled: true
    type: stdio
    name: edi
    cmd: /absolute/path/to/edi-mcp
    args: []
    envs:
      EDI_API_KEY: paste-your-key-here
    timeout: 300
```

## OpenCode

Add to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`[^opencode-mcp]. This is the 1.x layout;
OpenCode 2.x nests servers one level deeper, under `"mcp": {"servers": {…}}`, which is
what the install script writes when it detects 2.x.

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "edi": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["/absolute/path/to/edi-mcp", "--transport", "stdio"],
      "enabled": true,
      "environment": { "EDI_API_KEY": "paste-your-key-here" }
    }
  }
}
```

## VS Code

Add to `.vscode/mcp.json` in a workspace, or to your user configuration[^vscode-mcp].
An `inputs` prompt keeps the key out of the file:

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    { "type": "promptString", "id": "edi-api-key", "description": "EDI API key", "password": true }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "edi": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/edi-mcp",
      "args": ["--transport", "stdio"],
      "env": { "EDI_API_KEY": "${input:edi-api-key}" }
    }
  }
}
```

## Any other stdio client

Run `edi-mcp --transport stdio` (bare `edi-mcp` does the same) with the key in the
environment. The server speaks MCP 2026-07-28 and still accepts clients on earlier
protocol revisions over stdio.

## A hosted server (HTTP)

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http edi https://edi-mcp.example.org/mcp \
  --header "X-EDI-Key: $EDI_API_KEY"
```

Each user sends their own key in `X-EDI-Key`; the server honours it only when its
`public_base_url` is `https://` (see [Transports](../mcp/transports.md)). Over HTTP the
planned download tools are not offered.

[^claude-code-mcp]: Claude Code — MCP. <https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/mcp>
[^codex-mcp]: OpenAI Codex CLI. <https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/>
[^gemini-mcp]: Gemini CLI — MCP servers. <https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/tools/mcp-server.md>
[^goose-ext]: Goose — Using extensions. <https://block.github.io/goose/docs/getting-started/using-extensions>
[^opencode-mcp]: OpenCode — MCP servers. <https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/>
[^vscode-mcp]: VS Code — Use MCP servers. <https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/chat/mcp-servers>

# Configuration

edi-mcp runs with no configuration at all: the defaults serve stdio, cache upstream
responses in memory, keep tool results small and confine downloads to
`~/edi-downloads`. Settings come from four layers; a higher layer wins:

1. **Command-line flags** (only a handful of common settings).
2. **Environment variables** named `EDI_MCP_<SECTION>__<FIELD>`, with a double
   underscore descending into nested sections at any depth, for example
   `EDI_MCP_EDI__RETRIES__MAX_ATTEMPTS=5`. List settings take a comma-separated value:
   `EDI_MCP_SERVER__ALLOWED_HOSTS=edi.example.org,alt.example.org`. The empty string,
   `none` and `null` mean "unset".
3. **A YAML file** passed with `--config path.yaml`, using the same section and field
   names.
4. **Built-in defaults** (the table below).

Unknown keys in the YAML file or the environment are ignored with a warning, so a typo
does not stop the server but is visible in its log. The loader only checks the shape of
the settings; it never contacts EDI.

## The EDI API key

The key is the only secret, and it is read from the environment only. Set
`EDI_API_KEY`, the name EDI's own guides use. `EDI_MCP_EDI__API_KEY`, when set, takes
precedence (for giving edi-mcp a different key from your other EDI tools). Look-alike
names (`EDI_KEY`, `EDI_TOKEN`, `EDI_AUTH_TOKEN`) are **not** read; edi-mcp logs a
warning if one of them is set without `EDI_API_KEY`. There is deliberately **no
command-line flag** for the key: arguments are visible to every user in the process
list and end up in shell history. edi-mcp does not load `.env` files itself; if you
keep the key in one, export it into the environment before starting the server. See
[EDI API key](api-key.md) for creating a key and checking that EDI accepts it.

The key decides the backend: with one, edi-mcp reads PASTA; without one, it reads the
anonymous DataONE replicas ([Backends](../tools/backends.md)).

## Command-line flags

| Flag | Sets |
| --- | --- |
| `--config PATH` | YAML file to load |
| `--transport {stdio,http}` | `server.transport` |
| `--bind-address`, `--bind-port` | `server.bind_address`, `server.bind_port` |
| `--log-level` | `server.log_level` |
| `--download-dir PATH` | `downloads.directory` |
| `--no-downloads` | `downloads.enabled = false` |
| `--print-config` | print the effective configuration as YAML (key shown as `***`) and exit |
| `--check` | load the configuration, call `edi_ping` in-process (no network request), print a JSON report, exit 0 or 1 |
| `--version` | print the version |

## A YAML example

```yaml
# edi-mcp.yaml — pass with: edi-mcp --config edi-mcp.yaml
edi:
  max_concurrency: 4
  retries:
    max_attempts: 3
cache:
  ttl_s:
    search: 600
limits:
  max_result_bytes: 50000
downloads:
  directory: /data/edi-downloads
server:
  log_level: info
```

Never put the API key in a YAML file you share or commit; use `EDI_API_KEY`.

## Automatic values

A few settings default to "unset" and resolve per transport:

* `downloads.enabled`: downloads exist only on stdio; over HTTP the download tools are
  never listed, whatever this says. `--no-downloads` turns them off on stdio too. (The
  download tools themselves are still being built; see the
  [Roadmap](../tools/roadmap.md).)
* `server.dns_rebinding_protection`: unset follows the MCP SDK default, which is on for
  loopback binds or when `allowed_hosts` / `allowed_origins` are set.
* `server.public_base_url`: when set, its host and origin join the allow-lists, and an
  `https://` URL enables per-caller keys in the `X-EDI-Key` header (see
  [Hosted HTTP deployment](../deploy/hosted-http.md)).

## All settings

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED CONFIG (scripts/gen_config_reference.py; do not edit) -->

| Setting (YAML path) | Environment variable | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `edi.pasta_base_url` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__PASTA_BASE_URL` | str | `https://pasta.lternet.edu` | PASTA+ base URL (package and audit services). |
| `edi.auth_base_url` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__AUTH_BASE_URL` | str | `https://auth.edirepository.org/auth/v1` | EDI Identity and Access Manager API (key -> edi-token exchange). |
| `edi.dataone_cn_url` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__DATAONE_CN_URL` | str | `https://cn.dataone.org/cn/v2` | DataONE coordinating node (Solr search, resolve) used without a key. |
| `edi.gmn_lter_url` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__GMN_LTER_URL` | str | `https://gmn.lternet.edu/mn/v2` | DataONE member node serving knb-lter-* packages without a key. |
| `edi.gmn_edi_url` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__GMN_EDI_URL` | str | `https://gmn.edirepository.org/mn/v2` | DataONE member node serving edi.* and other non-LTER packages without a key. |
| `edi.cite_url` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__CITE_URL` | str | `https://cite.edirepository.org/cite` | EDI citation service (anonymous). |
| `edi.portal_url` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__PORTAL_URL` | str | `https://portal.edirepository.org/nis` | EDI Data Portal (landing pages are built from it). |
| `edi.api_key` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__API_KEY`<br>(or `EDI_API_KEY`) | SecretStr \| null | unset | EDI API access key (https://auth.edirepository.org/auth/ui/key). Enables the PASTA backend; without it edi-mcp uses DataONE. Prefer the EDI_API_KEY env var; never commit it. |
| `edi.user_agent_suffix` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__USER_AGENT_SUFFIX` | str \| null | unset | Text appended to the User-Agent header. |
| `edi.connect_timeout_s` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S` | float | `10.0` | TCP/TLS connect timeout. |
| `edi.read_timeout_s` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__READ_TIMEOUT_S` | float | `60.0` | Default read timeout. |
| `edi.download_read_timeout_s` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__DOWNLOAD_READ_TIMEOUT_S` | float | `300.0` | Read timeout for data-entity downloads. |
| `edi.max_concurrency` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__MAX_CONCURRENCY` | int | `4` | Maximum simultaneous upstream requests. |
| `edi.token_refresh_margin_s` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN_S` | float | `3600.0` | Refresh the 8-hour edi-token once fewer than this many seconds remain. |
| `edi.auth_fallback_s` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__AUTH_FALLBACK_S` | float | `300.0` | After the EDI auth service fails, send ?key= for this long before retrying it. |
| `edi.max_response_bytes` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` | int | `20971520` | Largest upstream response body read into memory. |
| `edi.retries.max_attempts` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__RETRIES__MAX_ATTEMPTS` | int | `3` | Attempts per upstream call, including the first. |
| `edi.retries.backoff_base_s` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__RETRIES__BACKOFF_BASE_S` | float | `0.5` | Base of the exponential backoff (0.5 * 2^n seconds). |
| `edi.retries.backoff_max_s` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__RETRIES__BACKOFF_MAX_S` | float | `8.0` | Cap on a single backoff sleep. |
| `edi.retries.retry_after_default_s` | `EDI_MCP_EDI__RETRIES__RETRY_AFTER_DEFAULT_S` | float | `1.0` | Wait used on HTTP 429 when no Retry-After header is sent. |
| `cache.enabled` | `EDI_MCP_CACHE__ENABLED` | bool | `true` | Cache upstream responses in memory. |
| `cache.max_entries` | `EDI_MCP_CACHE__MAX_ENTRIES` | int | `1024` | Overall entry cap across families. |
| `cache.stale_if_error_s` | `EDI_MCP_CACHE__STALE_IF_ERROR_S` | int | `86400` | How long an expired entry may be served when a refresh fails. |
| `cache.ttl_s.listings` | `EDI_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__LISTINGS` | int | `3600` | Scope, identifier and revision listings. |
| `cache.ttl_s.search` | `EDI_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__SEARCH` | int | `600` | Search results. |
| `cache.ttl_s.metadata` | `EDI_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__METADATA` | int | `86400` | EML and entity facts of a given revision (immutable upstream). |
| `cache.ttl_s.reports` | `EDI_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__REPORTS` | int | `86400` | Quality reports and provenance. |
| `cache.ttl_s.feeds` | `EDI_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__FEEDS` | int | `300` | Change and upload feeds, read counts. |
| `cache.ttl_s.citations` | `EDI_MCP_CACHE__TTL_S__CITATIONS` | int | `86400` | Formatted citations. |
| `limits.default_limit` | `EDI_MCP_LIMITS__DEFAULT_LIMIT` | int | `25` | Default page size where a tool does not set its own. |
| `limits.max_limit` | `EDI_MCP_LIMITS__MAX_LIMIT` | int | `200` | Largest page size any tool accepts. |
| `limits.max_result_bytes` | `EDI_MCP_LIMITS__MAX_RESULT_BYTES` | int | `50000` | Tool results are trimmed (with page.truncated) to fit this many bytes of compact JSON. |
| `limits.hard_max_result_bytes` | `EDI_MCP_LIMITS__HARD_MAX_RESULT_BYTES` | int | `200000` | A result still larger than this after trimming fails with result_too_large. |
| `limits.text_budget_summary` | `EDI_MCP_LIMITS__TEXT_BUDGET_SUMMARY` | int | `300` | Characters kept of long text fields (abstracts) in summaries. |
| `limits.text_budget_detail` | `EDI_MCP_LIMITS__TEXT_BUDGET_DETAIL` | int | `4000` | Default characters kept of long text fields in detail views. |
| `limits.max_eml_bytes` | `EDI_MCP_LIMITS__MAX_EML_BYTES` | int | `20971520` | Largest EML document parsed (larger ones fail with result_too_large). |
| `limits.preview_max_bytes` | `EDI_MCP_LIMITS__PREVIEW_MAX_BYTES` | int | `262144` | Most bytes edi_preview_entity reads from an entity. |
| `limits.tools_list_max_bytes` | `EDI_MCP_LIMITS__TOOLS_LIST_MAX_BYTES` | int | `60000` | Conformance bound on the serialized tools/list result; tightened once every tool lands. |
| `downloads.enabled` | `EDI_MCP_DOWNLOADS__ENABLED` | bool \| null | unset | Offer the download tools. Unset: true on stdio; never available over http. |
| `downloads.directory` | `EDI_MCP_DOWNLOADS__DIRECTORY` | Path | `~/edi-downloads` | Directory every download is confined to (created on first use). |
| `downloads.max_files_per_call` | `EDI_MCP_DOWNLOADS__MAX_FILES_PER_CALL` | int | `50` | Most entities one edi_download_entities call transfers. |
| `downloads.max_bytes_per_call` | `EDI_MCP_DOWNLOADS__MAX_BYTES_PER_CALL` | int | `2147483648` | Most bytes one download call transfers. |
| `downloads.max_file_bytes` | `EDI_MCP_DOWNLOADS__MAX_FILE_BYTES` | int | `1073741824` | Largest single file accepted. |
| `downloads.verify_checksums` | `EDI_MCP_DOWNLOADS__VERIFY_CHECKSUMS` | bool | `true` | Verify the SHA-1 checksums EDI publishes. |
| `downloads.allowed_hosts` | `EDI_MCP_DOWNLOADS__ALLOWED_HOSTS` | list[str] | `[pasta.lternet.edu, gmn.lternet.edu, gmn.edirepository.org, cn.dataone.org]` | Hosts downloads (and their redirects) may come from; '*.' is a subdomain wildcard. |
| `server.transport` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__TRANSPORT` | `stdio` \| `http` | `stdio` | stdio (local clients) or http (stateless Streamable HTTP at /mcp). |
| `server.bind_address` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__BIND_ADDRESS` | str | `127.0.0.1` | HTTP bind address. |
| `server.bind_port` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__BIND_PORT` | int | `8080` | HTTP bind port. |
| `server.public_base_url` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | str \| null | unset | Public URL of a hosted deployment; its host/origin join the allow-lists and https:// enables per-request keys. |
| `server.allowed_hosts` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__ALLOWED_HOSTS` | list[str] | `[]` | Host header allow-list (DNS-rebinding protection). |
| `server.allowed_origins` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | list[str] | `[]` | Origin header allow-list (DNS-rebinding protection). |
| `server.dns_rebinding_protection` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__DNS_REBINDING_PROTECTION` | bool \| null | unset | Force DNS-rebinding protection on/off. Unset: SDK default (on for loopback binds or when allow-lists are set). |
| `server.json_response` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__JSON_RESPONSE` | bool | `false` | Answer POST /mcp with application/json instead of a single SSE frame. |
| `server.max_request_body_size` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE` | int | `1048576` | Largest accepted request body in bytes. |
| `server.accept_header_key` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__ACCEPT_HEADER_KEY` | bool | `true` | HTTP: honour a per-request EDI API key header (subject to the TLS gate). |
| `server.request_key_header` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__REQUEST_KEY_HEADER` | str | `X-EDI-Key` | Header carrying a caller's EDI API key in HTTP mode. |
| `server.allow_insecure_header_key` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__ALLOW_INSECURE_HEADER_KEY` | bool | `false` | Accept header keys when public_base_url is not https:// (development only). |
| `server.share_config_key_over_http` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__SHARE_CONFIG_KEY_OVER_HTTP` | bool | `false` | Lend the operator's configured key to HTTP callers without one (private deployments only). |
| `server.tools_list_ttl_ms` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__TOOLS_LIST_TTL_MS` | int | `300000` | ttlMs advertised on tools/list. |
| `server.log_level` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__LOG_LEVEL` | `debug` \| `info` \| `warning` \| `error` \| `critical` | `info` | Log verbosity. |
| `server.instructions_extra` | `EDI_MCP_SERVER__INSTRUCTIONS_EXTRA` | str \| null | unset | Text appended to the server instructions. |

# Install edi-mcp

edi-mcp is a Python 3.11+ package with one command, `edi-mcp`, that MCP clients start
over stdio. These instructions cover macOS, Linux and Windows.

!!! note "No PyPI release yet"

    edi-mcp is under construction and has not been published to PyPI; the first
    release (v0.1.0) is the last step of the build plan, although the package already
    reports that version number. Until then, install from GitHub[^repo] as shown below.

## Prerequisites

- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/){target=_blank}[^uv], which installs Python 3.11+
  for edi-mcp if your system lacks it, and keeps the server in its own environment.
- git, for the install script and installs from source.
- Optional: an [EDI API key](api-key.md). Without one, edi-mcp answers from the
  anonymous DataONE replicas of EDI content.

Install uv[^uv-install]:

=== "macOS"

    ```bash
    curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
    # or: brew install uv
    ```

=== "Linux"

    ```bash
    curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
    ```

=== "Windows (PowerShell)"

    ```powershell
    powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
    # or: winget install --id=astral-sh.uv -e
    ```

Open a new terminal afterwards so `uv` is on your `PATH`.

## Option 1: From source with the install script (recommended)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp.git
cd edi-mcp
scripts/install.sh
```

`scripts/install.sh` creates the server environment (`uv sync`) if `.venv/bin/edi-mcp`
is missing, then registers that executable with every supported agent it finds on
your machine: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, OpenAI Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Goose and
OpenCode. It prefers each agent's own CLI when one is installed (`claude mcp add`,
`codex mcp add`, `gemini mcp add`) and otherwise merges an entry into the agent's
config file, keeping everything else in the file and leaving a `.bak` copy.

```bash
scripts/install.sh --with-key                    # also store your EDI API key (see below)
scripts/install.sh --agents all --dry-run        # preview the change for every agent
scripts/install.sh --agents claude,goose         # just Claude Code and Goose
scripts/install.sh --scope project               # project-level config (claude, codex, gemini, opencode)
scripts/install.sh --env EDI_MCP_SERVER__LOG_LEVEL=debug   # any extra environment variable
scripts/install.sh --command "$(command -v edi-mcp)"       # register a uv-tool install instead
scripts/install.sh --uninstall                   # remove the registration everywhere
```

| Agent | What the script does |
| --- | --- |
| `claude` (Claude Code) | `claude mcp add --scope user edi -- /path/to/edi-mcp/.venv/bin/edi-mcp` |
| `claude-desktop` | adds `mcpServers.edi` to `claude_desktop_config.json` |
| `codex` (OpenAI Codex CLI) | `codex mcp add edi -- …`, or an `[mcp_servers.edi]` table in `~/.codex/config.toml` |
| `gemini` (Gemini CLI) | `gemini mcp add --scope user edi …`, or `mcpServers.edi` in `~/.gemini/settings.json` |
| `goose` | adds an `edi` stdio extension to `~/.config/goose/config.yaml` |
| `opencode` | adds `mcp.servers.edi` (v2) or `mcp.edi` (v1) to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` |

The script writes the absolute path of the executable, because desktop apps do not
inherit your shell `PATH`. It needs bash; macOS's built-in bash 3.2 is enough. Restart
desktop apps (Claude Desktop, Goose Desktop) after installing.

### The EDI API key and the script

There is deliberately no option that takes the key itself, since command lines end
up in shell history and process lists. `--with-key` reads `EDI_API_KEY` from your
environment, or asks for it with hidden input, and writes it into each agent's server
`env`:

```bash
read -rs EDI_API_KEY && export EDI_API_KEY     # paste the key, press Enter
scripts/install.sh --with-key
```

- The key is then stored **in plain text** in each agent's config file. The script
  restricts the files it writes to your user (mode `600`) and never prints the key;
  dry runs show `***`.
- For agents registered through their own CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI), the
  key is passed to that CLI's `mcp add` command and is briefly visible in the process
  list. Add `--prefer-files` to have Codex and Gemini CLI configured by file instead.
- Without `--with-key` no key is stored, and the server uses the anonymous DataONE
  backend unless the agent passes `EDI_API_KEY` to it some other way.

### Windows

On Windows, register by hand (Option 2) or run the script from **Git Bash**, which
converts paths to Windows form and writes Claude Desktop's config under `%APPDATA%`.
Git Bash support has not been tested as widely as macOS and Linux; check the result
with `--dry-run` first. Do not run the script inside WSL to configure Windows apps:
it would write WSL's own config files, which Claude Desktop for Windows never reads.

## Option 2: Install the package and register it by hand

Install the `edi-mcp` command:

=== "uv tool (recommended)"

    ```bash
    uv tool install git+https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp
    ```

    This puts `edi-mcp` in uv's tool directory (`~/.local/bin` on macOS and Linux,
    `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` on Windows). Upgrade with `uv tool upgrade edi-mcp`.

=== "uvx (no install)"

    ```bash
    uvx --from git+https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp edi-mcp --version
    ```

    Clients can use `uvx` as the command with
    `["--from", "git+https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp", "edi-mcp"]` as its
    arguments; the first start is slower while uv builds the environment.

=== "pipx / pip"

    ```bash
    pipx install git+https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp
    # or, inside a virtual environment:
    pip install "git+https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp"
    ```

=== "From source"

    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp
    cd edi-mcp
    uv sync                      # creates .venv with the package
    uv run edi-mcp --version
    ```

Then find the executable's absolute path, which is what desktop apps need:

=== "macOS / Linux"

    ```bash
    command -v edi-mcp           # e.g. /Users/you/.local/bin/edi-mcp
    # from source: /path/to/edi-mcp/.venv/bin/edi-mcp
    ```

=== "Windows (PowerShell)"

    ```powershell
    (Get-Command edi-mcp).Source  # e.g. C:\Users\you\.local\bin\edi-mcp.exe
    # from source: C:\path\to\edi-mcp\.venv\Scripts\edi-mcp.exe
    ```

and register it with your client. The shortest form, for Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add edi -s user -e EDI_API_KEY="$EDI_API_KEY" -- edi-mcp
```

Claude Desktop, and other JSON-configured clients:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "edi": {
      "command": "/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/edi-mcp",
      "args": [],
      "env": { "EDI_API_KEY": "paste-your-key-here" }
    }
  }
}
```

Use absolute paths (not `~/` or `./`). On Windows escape backslashes:
`"C:\\Users\\You\\.local\\bin\\edi-mcp.exe"`. Leave out `env` to run without a key.
[Clients](clients.md) has the entries for Claude Desktop, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI,
Goose, OpenCode, VS Code and hosted servers.

## Option 3: Docker

A container image (`python:3.13-slim`, non-root, HTTP on port 8080 with a `/healthz`
check) is planned for the v0.1.0 release; see the [Roadmap](../tools/roadmap.md).
There is no Dockerfile yet.

## Verify the installation

```bash
edi-mcp --version     # edi-mcp 0.1.0
edi-mcp --check       # {"ok": true, "version": "0.1.0", "protocolVersion": "2026-07-28", "transport": "stdio", "keyConfigured": false, "backend": "dataone"}
```

`--check` loads your configuration, calls `edi_ping` in-process and prints a one-line
JSON report: the version, protocol, transport, whether an EDI API key is configured
and which backend that selects (`pasta` with a key, `dataone` without). It makes no
network request, so it does not prove that EDI accepts your key. For that, ask your
agent to call `edi_ping` with `check_api=true` once the server is connected; see
[EDI API key](api-key.md#check-the-key). `--print-config` shows the effective settings
with the key replaced by `***`.

In Claude Code, `claude mcp list` runs a health check and shows `edi` as connected. To
talk to the server directly over stdio:

```bash
# 2026-07-28 client: every request carries the protocol envelope in _meta
echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"server/discover","params":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion":"2026-07-28","io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities":{},"io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo":{"name":"manual","version":"0"}}}}' \
  | edi-mcp

# 2025-era client: classic initialize handshake, then tools/list
printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"manual","version":"0"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' \
  | edi-mcp
```

Both print JSON-RPC responses on stdout (logs go to stderr) and exit once stdin
closes. `server/discover` reports the server's capabilities and instructions; a
`tools/list` request with the same `_meta` envelope lists every tool (see the
[Tool reference](../tools/reference.md)).

## Configuration

Nothing is required. The settings most people touch:

```bash
EDI_API_KEY=                      # optional; PASTA with it, DataONE without
EDI_MCP_SERVER__LOG_LEVEL=info    # debug | info | warning | error | critical (stderr)
EDI_MCP_DOWNLOADS__DIRECTORY=     # where the planned download tools may write
```

edi-mcp does not read `.env` files on its own. See [Configuration](configuration.md)
for every setting, the YAML file and the precedence rules.

## Troubleshooting

**`edi-mcp: command not found` from a desktop app.** Desktop apps do not read your
shell profile. Use the executable's absolute path as the `command`; the install script
does this for you.

**Server shows as disconnected.** Run the configured command yourself with
`--check`. If it fails, re-create the environment (`uv sync` in a clone, or
`uv tool install --reinstall git+https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp`). Claude Desktop
logs live in `~/Library/Logs/Claude/` (macOS) or `%APPDATA%\Claude\logs\` (Windows);
in Claude Code, `claude mcp get edi` shows the connection status.

**`backend` is `dataone` although you have a key.** The key did not reach the server
process: desktop apps do not see variables exported in your shell. Put it in the
client's `env` block, or re-run the install script with `--with-key`.

**`upstream_forbidden` errors.** EDI refused the key; without a `reason` it is
mistyped, expired or deleted. With `reason: access_restricted` the key works but the
package is restricted. See [EDI API key](api-key.md#errors).

**Port already in use.** MCP over stdio uses no network port; a port error comes from
an HTTP deployment (`--transport http`, port 8080 by default) or something else on your
machine.

**Windows paths.** In JSON, write backslashes doubled (`C:\\Users\\…`) or use forward
slashes. Point at `edi-mcp.exe`, not the extension-less name.

## Upgrading

```bash
# install script / from source
git pull origin main && uv sync
# uv tool
uv tool upgrade edi-mcp
```

Registrations made by the install script keep pointing at `.venv/bin/edi-mcp`, so
`git pull && uv sync` is enough; restart desktop apps afterwards.

## Uninstallation

```bash
scripts/install.sh --uninstall   # remove the server from every agent config
cd .. && rm -rf edi-mcp          # if installed from source
uv tool uninstall edi-mcp        # if installed with uv tool
```

- [Quickstart](quickstart.md): a first session.
- [EDI API key](api-key.md): create a key and give it to edi-mcp.
- [Clients](clients.md): per-client configuration.
- [Configuration](configuration.md): every setting.

# Quickstart

This walks through a first session in Claude Code[^claude-code-mcp]; other clients
work the same way once connected ([Clients](clients.md)). It uses the tools available
today: `edi_ping`, the discovery tools (`edi_search_packages`, `edi_list_scopes`,
`edi_list_identifiers`, `edi_list_revisions`) and the package tools (`edi_get_package`,
`edi_get_metadata`, `edi_list_entities`). Preview, download and citation tools are still
being built; see the [Roadmap](../tools/roadmap.md).

## 1. Register the server

edi-mcp works with or without an EDI API key. With a key it reads EDI's own PASTA+ API;
without one it falls back to the anonymous DataONE replicas of EDI content (see
[Backends](../tools/backends.md)).

=== "With an EDI API key"

    Create a key at [auth.edirepository.org](https://auth.edirepository.org/auth/ui/key){target=_blank}
    ([step by step](api-key.md#create-a-key)) and export it as `EDI_API_KEY` without
    echoing it to the terminal:

    ```bash
    read -rs EDI_API_KEY && export EDI_API_KEY     # paste the key, press Enter
    claude mcp add edi -s user -e EDI_API_KEY="$EDI_API_KEY" -- edi-mcp --transport stdio
    ```

=== "Without a key"

    ```bash
    claude mcp add edi -s user -- edi-mcp --transport stdio
    ```

    Search and the listing tools answer from DataONE, which can lag new EDI uploads.
    `edi_list_scopes` then serves a dated snapshot instead of the live list.

## 2. Check it

Ask the agent to "call edi_ping with check_api=true". The result shows the version,
protocol `2026-07-28`, `keyConfigured`, the `backend` serving you (`pasta` or
`dataone`) and, under `api`, whether one small request to that backend succeeded. With
a key, `api.credential` is `token` when edi-mcp exchanged the key for a short-lived
`edi-token`. The key itself never appears in any result.

## 3. Find and inspect a package

The agent normally chains these on its own; the arguments below are what it sends.
Results are abbreviated, and the package ids are examples: what a search returns
depends on the backend and on what EDI holds at the time.

1. **Search**

    ```json
    {"tool": "edi_search_packages", "arguments": {"query": "net primary production", "scope": "Jornada"}}
    ```

    → `resolved: [{"field": "scope", "input": "Jornada", "code": "knb-lter-jrn", ...}]`
    and `items`, each with `packageId` (such as `knb-lter-jrn.210548103.33`), `title`,
    `pubDate`, `doi`, `authors`, `keywords` and `portalUrl`, plus `page` for paging and
    `source.backend`. Scopes accept exact names (`knb-lter-jrn`), LTER site codes (`JRN`)
    and names (`Jornada`); see [Package identifiers](../tools/identifiers.md).

2. **List the revisions of one package**

    ```json
    {"tool": "edi_list_revisions", "arguments": {"package": "jrn.210548103"}}
    ```

    → `series: "knb-lter-jrn.210548103"`, the `revisions` in ascending order, `newest`,
    `oldest` and `newestPackageId`. Without a key, DataONE answers and may not yet hold
    the newest revision PASTA has.

3. **Browse a scope**

    ```json
    {"tool": "edi_list_identifiers", "arguments": {"scope": "HBR"}}
    ```

    → the package identifiers in `knb-lter-hbr`, ascending and paged.

4. **Read one package**

    ```json
    {"tool": "edi_get_package", "arguments": {"package": "knb-lter-hbr.14.22"}}
    ```

    → `title`, `doi`, `license`, `isNewest`, and `entities` with sizes and
    `totalBytes`. Then `edi_get_metadata` (with `include` such as
    `["overview", "coverage"]`) gives the abstract, keywords and coverage, and
    `edi_list_entities` gives each table's columns, units and missing-value codes,
    with a PASTA `dataUrl` and, where DataONE replicates the scope, a keyless
    `anonymousUrl`. See [Packages, metadata and entities](../tools/packages.md).

Every result also carries `notes` (caveats such as DataONE lag) and `nextSteps`
(concrete follow-up calls). The [Tool reference](../tools/reference.md) lists every
input and result field.

[^claude-code-mcp]: Claude Code — MCP. <https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/mcp>
[^pasta-api]: EDI PASTA+ Data Package Manager REST API. <https://pasta.lternet.edu/package/docs/api>

# Backends: PASTA and DataONE

Since **2026-07-30** every request to EDI's PASTA+ REST API must be authenticated,
including reads of public data[^edi-news-auth]; an anonymous request gets HTTP 403
("Public Access … not authorized"). DataONE still serves EDI content anonymously, so
edi-mcp has two backends behind one contract:

| | PASTA | DataONE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Used when | the call has an EDI API key | the call has no key |
| Search and listings | `pasta.lternet.edu/package/search/eml` and `/package/eml/…` | the coordinating node's Solr index, `cn.dataone.org/cn/v2/query/solr/` |
| EML and data | `pasta.lternet.edu/package/…` | the member node holding the scope (`gmn.edirepository.org` for `edi`, `gmn.lternet.edu` otherwise), then `cn.dataone.org` as a fallback |
| Freshness | authoritative | replicas; new uploads can take days to appear |

Each tool produces the same output model from either backend, and every result's
`source.backend` says which one answered: `pasta` or `dataone`, or `local` when
no upstream call was made. [`edi_ping`](reference.md#edi_ping) reports the backend that
serves the current caller.

## A bad key is an error, never a downgrade

If a key is configured and PASTA rejects it (HTTP 401), the tool fails with
`upstream_forbidden`; edi-mcp does **not** quietly retry on DataONE, because a silent
downgrade would hide the misconfiguration and change what the results mean. A 403
with valid credentials means the package is restricted to named users or groups; it
is also `upstream_forbidden`, with `reason: access_restricted`, and a new key will not
help. See [Utilities and errors](utilities.md#error-codes).

One deliberate exception keeps answers correct rather than changing their source:
PASTA's search indexes only the newest revision of each package, so a DOI of an
older revision is resolved through DataONE even with a key, and the result's notes
say so.

## Key-only operations

Some EDI services have no DataONE counterpart: quality reports, provenance
(lineage), change and upload feeds, read counts and whole-package zip downloads. The
tools planned for them (see the [Roadmap](roadmap.md)) will return `auth_required`
without a key. [`edi_list_scopes`](reference.md#edi_list_scopes) needs PASTA for a
live list and falls back to edi-mcp's dated scope snapshot without a key.

## Caveats of the DataONE fallback

* **Lag.** The DataONE index can trail new EDI uploads and new revisions by a day or
  more. Results served from DataONE carry a note saying so.
* **Coverage.** Not every EDI scope is replicated to DataONE;
  [`edi_list_scopes`](reference.md#edi_list_scopes) shows DataONE package counts from
  the snapshot, and a scope with none needs a key.
* **Revisions.** DataONE's obsolescence links are unreliable, so edi-mcp parses each
  record's revision from its identifier, keeps the highest revision per package,
  and reports search totals as an upper bound (`totalExact: false`).
* **Proxying.** The member nodes proxy PASTA, so EDI could restrict them in the same
  way it restricted PASTA.
* **Drift.** DataONE's index changes without notice: which scopes are replicated,
  which fields can be sorted, and the order of results for filter-only queries have
  all changed while edi-mcp was being built. Do not rely on DataONE's result order,
  and set a key when you need authoritative answers.

[^edi-news-auth]: EDI news, 2026-07-27. <https://edirepository.org/news/news-20260727.00>

# Discovery

Four tools find packages and walk the repository's hierarchy of
**scope → identifier → revision**. All four work with or without an EDI API key:
with a key PASTA answers, without one the anonymous DataONE replicas do (see
[Backends](backends.md)). Every scope argument accepts an exact scope
(`knb-lter-jrn`), an LTER site code (`JRN`) or a name such as `Jornada`; see
[Identifiers and scope names](identifiers.md).

| Tool | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| [`edi_search_packages`](reference.md#edi_search_packages) | find packages by text, scope, creator, years or bounding box |
| [`edi_list_scopes`](reference.md#edi_list_scopes) | see every scope with its name, kind, site code and package counts |
| [`edi_list_identifiers`](reference.md#edi_list_identifiers) | list the package identifiers in one scope |
| [`edi_list_revisions`](reference.md#edi_list_revisions) | list every revision of one package and find the newest |

## Search packages

`edi_search_packages` returns the **newest revision** of each matching package with
its title, DOI, publication date, temporal coverage, the first five creators
(`moreAuthors` counts the rest), the first ten keywords and an EDI Data Portal link.

| Input | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `query` | Free text over titles, keywords and abstracts: words, `"phrases"`, `AND` / `OR` / `NOT`. Omit it to browse with filters only. |
| `scope` | One scope, site code or scope name. |
| `author` | A creator's last name, any case (`Likens`). |
| `start_year`, `end_year` | Temporal overlap: coverage reaches `start_year` or later and starts in `end_year` or earlier. |
| `bbox` | `[west, south, east, north]` in decimal degrees; geographic coverage must intersect it. `west <= east`: split a box that crosses the antimeridian into two searches. |
| `sort` | `relevance` (default), `newest` or `oldest` by publication date (by DataONE upload date without a key). `oldest` lists undated packages first. |
| `include_bulk` | Include the generated bulk scopes `ecotrends`, `lter-landsat` and `lter-landsat-ledaps` (about 36,000 records), which are left out of unscoped searches by default. |
| `limit`, `offset` | Page size (1–50, default 10) and the index of the first result. |

Example: Hubbard Brook streamflow packages that cover the 1990s:

```json
{"query": "streamflow", "scope": "Hubbard Brook", "start_year": 1990, "end_year": 1999}
```

The scope name is resolved to `knb-lter-hbr` and echoed in `resolved` with its
confidence.

### PASTA and DataONE differences

The same filters are sent to both backends, but the two indexes are not identical:

* **Totals.** On PASTA `page.total` is exact. On DataONE `totalExact` is `false`:
  DataONE still counts some superseded revisions, which edi-mcp collapses to one hit
  per package, so `page.total` is an upper bound and a page can hold fewer than
  `limit` packages. A package can reappear on a later page at a higher revision.
* **Paging.** `page.nextOffset` advances by the rows requested (`offset + limit`),
  not by the hits kept, so no DataONE rows are read twice.
* **Freshness.** The DataONE index can lag new EDI uploads by days; results say so
  in `notes`.
* **Publication date.** PASTA returns a year, DataONE a date.
* **Date sorting.** Since 2026-10-19 DataONE refuses to sort on publication date,
  so without a key `sort=newest` and `sort=oldest` order results by the date each
  revision reached DataONE (`uploaded` on each hit), and a note says so. PASTA sorts
  by publication date.
* **Identifier forms.** DataONE returns some records under an older
  `scope.identifier.revision` id form; edi-mcp reads both and de-duplicates per
  package series.

## List scopes

`edi_list_scopes` lists the repository's scopes (`knb-lter-hbr`, `edi`, `msb-paleon`,
…) with name, `kind` (`lter`, `edi`, `bulk`, `project`, `agency`, `other`), LTER site
code, location and package counts on PASTA and DataONE. Filter with `kind`.

* **With a key** the scope list comes live from PASTA (`live: true`). Names and
  counts still come from edi-mcp's dated snapshot (`snapshotAsOf`); a scope newer
  than the snapshot has `kind: unknown`.
* **Without a key** DataONE has no scope listing, so the list is the snapshot
  itself (`live: false`), and scopes created since then are missing. The same
  snapshot is the `edi://reference/scopes` resource.

`dataonePackages: 0` means DataONE does not replicate that scope; reading it needs a
key.

## List identifiers

`edi_list_identifiers(scope=...)` lists a scope's numeric package identifiers in
ascending order, 200 per page by default (up to 1,000). A scope with no packages
returns `not_found`.

## List revisions

`edi_list_revisions(package=...)` lists every revision of one package, ascending,
with `newest`, `oldest` and `newestPackageId`. `package` accepts a series
(`knb-lter-hbr.14`), any revision (`knb-lter-hbr.14.22`), a DOI, or a portal or
PASTA URL, and the scope part may be a site code or name (`jrn.210548103`).
Revision numbers can start at 0.

Without a key the revisions come from DataONE, which can lag a new revision; edi-mcp
reads the revision from each record's identifier instead of DataONE's obsolescence
links, which are unreliable.

## Pagination

Search and identifier listings are paginated with `offset` and `limit`. Every page
reports `page.total` (when known), `returned`, `truncated` and `nextOffset`; when
`nextOffset` is set, the result's `nextSteps` include the call for the next page.
A result that would exceed the size budget is trimmed and reports
`truncatedReason: budget`.

# Identifiers and scope names

## Anatomy of a package id

An EDI data package is identified by **scope.identifier.revision**:

| Part | Example | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| scope | `knb-lter-hbr`, `edi` | Namespace: `knb-lter-<site>` for each LTER site (hbr = Hubbard Brook, jrn = Jornada, ntl = North Temperate Lakes, …), `edi` for general EDI submissions, and others such as `msb-paleon` or `ecotrends`. |
| identifier | `14`, `210548103` | Integer, unique within the scope. |
| revision | `22` | Integer, incremented on every update. Older revisions stay available. Revisions can start at 0 (`msb-paleon.31.0`). |

`knb-lter-hbr.14.22` is revision 22 of package 14 in the Hubbard Brook scope; the
path form is `knb-lter-hbr/14/22`. `knb-lter-hbr.14` (no revision) is the package
*series*. `newest` and `oldest` stand for the latest and the first revision.

## Other identifiers

* **DOI.** Every revision has its own DOI, `doi:10.6073/pasta/<32 hex>`, resolvable
  at `https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/<32 hex>`.
* **Landing page.**
  `https://portal.edirepository.org/nis/mapbrowse?scope=knb-lter-hbr&identifier=14&revision=22`
  (search results carry it as `portalUrl`).
* **Data entity.** A package's tables and files are *entities*, each with a 32-hex
  entity id (the MD5 of its EML `entityName`), addressed as
  `https://pasta.lternet.edu/package/data/eml/knb-lter-hbr/14/22/<entityId>`.
* **DataONE.** In DataONE the EML document's identifier is its PASTA metadata URL
  (`https://pasta.lternet.edu/package/metadata/eml/knb-lter-hbr/14/22`) and the
  package's resource map is its DOI.

## Forms edi-mcp accepts

Wherever a tool takes a package (today
[`edi_list_revisions`](reference.md#edi_list_revisions)), any of these work, and the
normalized id is echoed in `resolved` when it differs from the input:

* `knb-lter-hbr.14.22`, `knb-lter-hbr/14/22`, with an optional `.xml` suffix as in
  DataONE file names;
* `knb-lter-hbr.14`, `knb-lter-hbr.14.newest`, `knb-lter-hbr.14.oldest`;
* `doi:10.6073/pasta/…`, `10.6073/pasta/…`, `https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/…`
  (also `dx.doi.org`);
* portal URLs: `…/nis/mapbrowse?scope=…&identifier=…&revision=…` or
  `…?packageid=scope.identifier.revision`;
* PASTA package, metadata and data URLs, also when URL-encoded inside a DataONE
  `/object/` or `/resolve/` URL;
* a site code or scope name in place of the scope: `jrn.210548103`,
  `Jornada Basin.210548103.33`.

A DOI outside `10.6073/pasta/` is rejected with `invalid_argument`: only EDI DOIs
identify EDI packages. A DOI is turned into a package id by the backend; with a key,
PASTA's search finds the newest revision's DOI and an older revision's DOI is looked
up in DataONE (the result's notes say so).

## Scope names and site codes

Scope arguments (`scope=` and the scope part of a package id) accept, in this order:

1. the **exact scope**: `knb-lter-jrn`, `edi`, `msb-cap`;
2. an **LTER site code**, any case: `JRN`, `hbr`. Three-letter codes always mean
   the LTER site, so `cap` is Central Arizona-Phoenix (`knb-lter-cap`); use
   `msb-cap` exactly for the Macrosystems scope;
3. a **name, alias or location**, scored alike: `Jornada`, `Hubbard Brook`,
   `Toolik`, `Kansas`;
4. a **hyphenated code** edi-mcp does not know passes through unchanged, so scopes
   newer than the snapshot still work with a key.

A name match is accepted when it is clear — a score of at least **0.75** and at least
**1.15 times** the runner-up — and is echoed in `resolved` with its confidence. A
name or location shared by several scopes returns `ambiguous_input` with ranked
`candidates` (`Alaska` matches four sites, `New Mexico` both Jornada and Sevilleta,
`Landsat` two bulk scopes); a name that matches nothing well returns `not_found`
with `didYouMean`.

Names, site codes and locations come from a dated snapshot of the repository's
scopes shipped with edi-mcp (`edi://reference/scopes`).
[`edi_list_scopes`](reference.md#edi_list_scopes) lists every scope, live from
PASTA when a key is set.

# Packages, metadata and entities

Once a search or listing has named a package, three tools read it:
[`edi_get_package`](reference.md#edi_get_package) for an overview,
[`edi_get_metadata`](reference.md#edi_get_metadata) for the EML metadata, and
[`edi_list_entities`](reference.md#edi_list_entities) for the data tables and
files. All three take the same `package` and `revision` inputs, work on both
backends (PASTA with a key, DataONE without; see [Backends](backends.md)), and
fetch and parse the package's EML document once per call.

## Choosing a package and revision

`package` accepts every form described in [Identifiers and scope names](identifiers.md):
a full id (`knb-lter-hbr.14.22`), a series without a revision (`knb-lter-hbr.14`),
a DOI (`doi:10.6073/pasta/…`), a portal or PASTA URL, and a scope written as a site
code or name (`jrn.210548103`, `Jornada Basin.210548103`). When the package names
no revision, `revision` picks one: a number, `newest` (the default) or `oldest`.
Revision `0` is valid; some packages start there. Every result echoes the
normalised `packageId` and says in `revisionFrom` how the revision was chosen
(`given`, `newest`, `oldest` or `doi`).

## edi_get_package

The overview of one revision: `title`, `pubDate`, `creators` (names, with
`creatorsTotal`), `license`, `doi` and `doiUrl`, `portalUrl`, `metadataUrl`, and
`entities` with each entity's name, type and size, plus `entityCount` and
`totalBytes` across all entities.

- `newestRevision` and `isNewest` compare with the newest revision **on the backend
  that answered**. DataONE can lag PASTA, so without a key a note says that
  "newest" means DataONE's newest; PASTA may already hold a later revision.
- At most 100 entities are listed. A package with more says so in `notes` and
  `nextSteps` points at `edi_list_entities` with `offset=100` for the rest.
- `metadataUrl` is PASTA's EML URL, which needs an EDI API key to open.

## edi_get_metadata

The EML document projected into compact, capped sections. `include` picks the
sections (all by default):

| Section | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `overview` | title, short name, abstract, keyword sets (with thesauri), publication date, language, alternate identifiers, maintenance |
| `people` | creators, contacts, associated parties and publisher, with roles, organisations, emails as published, and ORCIDs |
| `coverage` | geographic bounding boxes, temporal ranges and taxonomic coverage |
| `methods` | the method steps as prose, with the number of steps |
| `rights` | intellectual rights text and the structured license (name, URL, identifier) |
| `project` | project title, personnel, funding awards and related projects |
| `entities` | the data entities in summary form (use `edi_list_entities` for columns) |

`max_text_chars` (200–20000, default 2000) cuts the abstract, methods and rights
text; a cut field is flagged (for example `abstractTruncated`). Lists are capped
(25 people per list, 60 keywords, 50 taxa, 25 geographic and temporal ranges, …)
and every capped list reports its full count, such as `keywordsTotal`. EML
`<references>` to other elements are resolved, with a depth limit and a cycle guard.
Very large documents stay small: the largest EML tried, 3.4 MB with more than a
thousand taxa, projects to about 25 KB.

The raw EML is never returned inline.

## edi_list_entities

Every data entity (data table, spatial raster or vector, stored procedure, view or
other entity) with:

- name, entity type, object (file) name, description, format, byte size and record count;
- the text format of a delimited table: header and footer lines, field and record delimiters
  (as written in the EML, for example the literal `\r\n`), quote character and orientation;
- with `include_attributes` (default true), each column's name, label, definition,
  storage type, measurement scale, unit, date format, numeric bounds, code lists,
  missing-value codes and semantic annotations;
- with `include_checksums`, SHA-1 checksums fetched for up to 25 entities per call
  (one request per entity); without it, checksums appear only where the backend
  already supplied them;
- `dataUrl`, PASTA's data URL, which needs an EDI API key, and `anonymousUrl`, a
  DataONE member-node URL that serves the same bytes without a key. `anonymousUrl`
  is omitted for scopes that the server's dated snapshot shows DataONE does not
  replicate.

`entity` narrows the list to one entity by id, name or file name
(case-insensitive). `offset` and `limit` (default 50, at most 200) page through
large packages, and `page.nextOffset` gives the next page. If a page would exceed
the result budget, column lists are dropped first and `attributesElided` is set;
ask for fewer entities or one `entity` to get them back.

## Typical flow

1. `edi_search_packages` → pick a `packageId`.
2. `edi_get_package` → is it the newest revision, how many entities, how big?
3. `edi_get_metadata` with `include=["overview","coverage","methods"]` → is it the
   right data?
4. `edi_list_entities` with `entity=…` → which columns, units and missing-value
   codes, and where to fetch the file.

Previewing rows, downloading files and formatted citations come with the next
build step; see the [Roadmap](roadmap.md).

# Tool reference

Generated from the tool registry by `scripts/gen_tools_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. 8 tools are registered. Inputs are snake_case and outputs camelCase. Every result also carries `resolved`, `notes`, `nextSteps` and `source` (whose `backend` says whether PASTA or DataONE answered), and failures return `structuredContent.error` with a stable `code` (see [Utilities](utilities.md#error-codes)).

| Tool | Title | Family | EDI API key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`edi_get_metadata`](#edi_get_metadata) | Read a package's EML metadata | [packages](packages.md) | no |
| [`edi_get_package`](#edi_get_package) | Get an EDI data package | [packages](packages.md) | no |
| [`edi_list_entities`](#edi_list_entities) | List a package's data entities | [entities](packages.md) | no |
| [`edi_list_identifiers`](#edi_list_identifiers) | List package identifiers in a scope | [discovery](discovery.md) | no |
| [`edi_list_revisions`](#edi_list_revisions) | List the revisions of a package | [discovery](discovery.md) | no |
| [`edi_list_scopes`](#edi_list_scopes) | List EDI scopes | [discovery](discovery.md) | no |
| [`edi_ping`](#edi_ping) | Check edi-mcp status | [core](utilities.md) | no |
| [`edi_search_packages`](#edi_search_packages) | Search EDI data packages | [discovery](discovery.md) | no |

## edi_get_metadata

**Read a package's EML metadata.** The package's EML, projected to compact sections: overview (abstract, keywords, dates), people (creators, contacts with ORCIDs), coverage (bounding boxes, date ranges, taxa), methods, rights and license, project and funding, and entities. Choose sections with include; long text is cut at max_text_chars and lists are capped with totals. Next: call edi_list_entities for column definitions, units and codes.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Surface | `packages` |
| EDI API key | optional (PASTA with a key, DataONE without) |
| Transports | http, stdio |
| Annotations | readOnly=true, destructive=false, idempotent=true, openWorld=true |
| Upstream endpoints | `GET pasta.lternet.edu/package/metadata/eml/{scope}/{id}/{rev}`<br>`GET gmn.lternet.edu/mn/v2/object/{pid}`<br>`GET pasta.lternet.edu/package/eml/{scope}/{id}`<br>`GET cn.dataone.org/cn/v2/query/solr/` |

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `package` | string | yes |  | A package: knb-lter-hbr.14.22, knb-lter-hbr.14 (newest unless revision is set), a DOI, or a portal or PASTA URL; the scope may be a site code or name (jrn.210548103). (min length 1; max length 500) |
| `revision` | integer \\| `newest` \\| `oldest` \\| null |  | null | Revision when package names none: a number, 'newest' (default) or 'oldest'. |
| `include` | array of `overview` \\| `people` \\| `coverage` \\| `methods` \\| `rights` \\| `project` \\| `entities` |  |  | Sections to return: overview (abstract, keywords, dates), people, coverage (geographic, temporal, taxonomic), methods, rights, project (funding), entities. Default: all. (min items 1) |
| `max_text_chars` | integer |  | `2000` | Cut abstract, methods and rights to this length. (>= 200; <= 20000) |

**Result fields** (besides the common envelope)

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packageId` | string |  |
| `revisionFrom` | `given` \\| `newest` \\| `oldest` \\| `doi` |  |
| `emlVersion` | string \\| null |  |
| `title` | string \\| null |  |
| `shortName` | string \\| null |  |
| `abstract` | string \\| null |  |
| `abstractTruncated` | boolean \\| null |  |
| `keywords` | array of KeywordSet \\| null |  |
| `keywordsTotal` | integer \\| null |  |
| `pubDate` | string \\| null |  |
| `language` | string \\| null |  |
| `alternateIdentifiers` | array of string \\| null |  |
| `maintenance` | string \\| null |  |
| `creators` | array of Person \\| null |  |
| `creatorsTotal` | integer \\| null |  |
| `contacts` | array of Person \\| null |  |
| `associatedParties` | array of Person \\| null |  |
| `publisher` | Person \\| null |  |
| `coverage` | Coverage \\| null |  |

## edi_get_package

**Get an EDI data package.** Overview of one package revision: title, publication date, creators, license, DOI, portal and metadata URLs, whether it is the newest revision, and its data entities with sizes and the total. Accepts package ids, series (newest unless revision is set), DOIs, portal or PASTA URLs, and site codes or scope names for the scope. Next: call edi_get_metadata for the full description or edi_list_entities for columns.

**List a package's data entities.** Every data entity (table or file) of one package revision: name, type, file name, format, byte size, record count, CSV layout and the columns with definitions, storage types, units, date formats, code lists and missing-value codes; optional SHA-1 checksums. ## edi_ping

**Check edi-mcp status.** Liveness and capability report: server version and protocol, whether an EDI API key is available and therefore which backend serves this caller (pasta with a key, dataone without), which tools need a key, and whether downloads are enabled. Never reveals the key. With check_api=true it also makes one small request to that backend to confirm the key and connectivity. Next: call edi_search_packages to find data packages.

## edi_search_packages

**Search EDI data packages.** Search EDI/LTER data packages by free text, scope (exact, LTER site code or name such as 'Jornada'), creator last name, temporal overlap (start_year/end_year) and bounding box; sort by relevance or publication date; paginated (offset/limit). Returns the newest revision of each package with title, DOI, coverage dates, creators and keywords. Bulk generated scopes are excluded unless include_bulk=true. Next: call edi_get_package or edi_get_metadata with a packageId.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string \\| null |  | null | Free text over titles, keywords and abstracts (words, "phrases", AND/OR/NOT). Omit to browse with filters only. (max length 500) |
| `scope` | string \\| null |  | null | Only this scope. A scope (knb-lter-jrn), LTER site code (JRN) or scope name or location ('Jornada', 'Hubbard Brook'); see edi_list_scopes. (max length 100) |
| `author` | string \\| null |  | null | A creator's last name, e.g. 'Likens' (any case). (max length 100) |
| `start_year` | integer \\| null |  | null | Temporal coverage reaches this year or later. (>= 1000; <= 2200) |
| `end_year` | integer \\| null |  | null | Temporal coverage starts in this year or earlier. (>= 1000; <= 2200) |
| `bbox` | array of number \\| null |  | null | [west, south, east, north] in decimal degrees; geographic coverage must intersect it. west <= east (no antimeridian crossing). (min items 4; max items 4) |
| `sort` | `relevance` \\| `newest` \\| `oldest` |  | `"relevance"` | relevance, or publication date: newest or oldest (oldest lists undated packages first). |

| `limit` | integer |  | `10` | Packages per page (1-50). (>= 1; <= 50) |

# Roadmap

edi-mcp is built in seven steps, one pull request each. Steps 1–5 are released on
`main`: the scaffold and auth probe, the MCP core (registry, transports, `edi_ping`,
conformance tests), the EDI client with both backends, the four
[discovery tools](discovery.md), and the [package, metadata and entity tools](packages.md). Everything on this page is **planned and not yet
available**; tool names and inputs may still change. The [tool reference](reference.md)
lists only what is registered today.

## Step 6 — previews, downloads, citations and key-only services

| Planned tool | Purpose | Key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `edi_preview_entity` | The first rows of a tabular entity, read with a byte cap. | optional |
| `edi_download_entities` | Save data entities under the configured download directory and verify their SHA-1. stdio only. | optional |
| `edi_download_package` | Save a whole package as a zip. stdio only. | required |
| `edi_get_citation` | A formatted citation (ESIP, DRYAD or BibTeX) from `cite.edirepository.org`. | optional |
| `edi_get_quality_report` | A summary of PASTA's congruence checks for a package. | required |
| `edi_get_lineage` | Provenance: a package's sources and descendants. | required |
| `edi_recent_changes` | Recent inserts, updates and deletes, by date or scope. | required |
| `edi_get_read_counts` | Download and read counts for a package. | required |

"Required" tools have no DataONE counterpart and will return `auth_required` without
a key (see [Backends](backends.md)). Downloads will be the only tools that write,
will never overwrite, and will be offered only over stdio.

## Step 7 — resources, prompts and release

* More `edi://` guides and references, and resource templates for a package and its
  raw EML.
* Prompts for finding data, citing a package and planning a download.
* A `server.json` for the MCP Registry, a Docker image, and the **v0.1.0** release
  on PyPI.

# Utilities and errors

## edi_ping

[`edi_ping`](reference.md#edi_ping) is a liveness and capability report. It makes no
upstream request unless asked to, so it is the first thing to call when a client
connects or a tool fails unexpectedly.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pong` | Always `ok`. |
| `version`, `protocolVersion` | edi-mcp version and the MCP revision it serves (`2026-07-28`). |
| `transport` | `stdio` or `http`. |
| `keyConfigured` | Whether this call has an EDI API key available. The key itself is never shown. |
| `keySource` | `config` (the server's environment or config file), `request` (an HTTP caller's `X-EDI-Key` header) or `none`. |
| `backend` | `pasta` with a key, `dataone` without one (see [Backends](backends.md)). |
| `keyRequiredTools` | Registered tools that fail with `auth_required` without a key. |
| `downloadsEnabled`, `downloadDir` | Whether download tools are offered on this transport, and where they write. |
| `endpoints` | The PASTA, auth, DataONE and citation base URLs in use. |
| `api` | Present only with `check_api=true`. |

With `check_api=true` edi-mcp makes one small request to the backend serving the
caller — with a key, it exchanges the key for a token and lists PASTA's scopes;
without one, it runs a zero-row DataONE query — and reports in `api`:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `reachable` | Whether the backend answered. |
| `backend` | The backend that was checked. |
| `credential` | `token` (an `edi-token` cookie), `key` (the key as a query parameter, used only when EDI's auth service is unreachable) or `none` (DataONE). |
| `endpoint`, `latencyMs` | The request made and how long it took. |
| `error` | The error `code` and `message` when the check failed, e.g. `upstream_forbidden` for a rejected key. |

`edi-mcp --check` calls `edi_ping` in-process and prints the report as JSON. It
stays offline; the live check is `edi_ping(check_api=true)`.

## Error codes

A failed tool call returns `isError: true` and
`structuredContent.error = {code, message, details, hint?}`. `code` is stable and
machine-readable; `message` is safe to show a user and never contains a key or token;
`hint`, when present, is a one-line remedy.

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_argument` | The arguments failed validation, an identifier could not be parsed, or the upstream rejected the request (HTTP 400). | Fix the argument; `details` names the problem and, for identifiers, lists the accepted forms. |
| `not_found` | No such package, scope, revision or resource (HTTP 404/410), or a scope name matched nothing. | Check the identifier; scope misses include `didYouMean`. |
| `ambiguous_input` | A scope name or location matches several scopes about equally. | Pick one of the ranked `candidates` and pass its exact scope. |
| `auth_required` | The operation needs an EDI API key and none is available for this call. | Set `EDI_API_KEY` (stdio) or send `X-EDI-Key` (HTTP); `details.guide` points at `edi://guide/api-key`. |
| `upstream_forbidden` | A key was sent and EDI refused. Without `reason` (HTTP 401) the key was rejected; with `reason: access_restricted` (HTTP 403) the key works but the package is restricted to named users or groups. | Replace the key, or for a restricted package ask its contact for access. edi-mcp never falls back to DataONE here. |
| `rate_limited` | The upstream answered HTTP 429. | Wait `details.retryAfterSeconds` before retrying. |
| `upstream_error` | The upstream failed (HTTP 5xx), answered with an unexpected status, or returned a body that could not be parsed. | Retry later; `details` carries the status and endpoint. |
| `upstream_unavailable` | The upstream could not be reached (network error or timeout). | Retry in a moment; call `edi_ping(check_api=true)`. |
| `result_too_large` | A result stayed above the hard size limit after trimming, or an upstream response exceeded the byte cap. | Narrow the request: a smaller `limit` or a narrower search. |
| `unknown_tool` | No tool has that name. | `details.available` lists the tools. |
| `internal_error` | A bug in edi-mcp. | Report it with the request id. |
| `feature_unavailable` | Reserved: a feature disabled by configuration. | — |
| `not_available_in_http_mode` | Reserved for the stdio-only download tools ([Roadmap](roadmap.md)). | Use a stdio deployment. |
| `download_limit_exceeded`, `download_denied`, `checksum_mismatch` | Reserved for the download tools ([Roadmap](roadmap.md)): a per-call limit, a path or host outside what is allowed, and a file whose SHA-1 differs from the one EDI publishes. | — |

Results that are merely large are not errors: lists are trimmed to fit the result
budget (50,000 bytes by default) and report `page.truncatedReason: budget` with a
`nextOffset` to continue from.

# MCP 2026-07-28 conformance

edi-mcp targets the **2026-07-28** revision of the Model Context Protocol, the
*stateless core*[^mcp-spec], on the Python `mcp` SDK 2.x (2.3.0 today) through its
low-level `Server` API[^python-sdk]. `server.py` is the only module coupled to the
SDK; the tool registry is SDK-agnostic.

## What the server does

| Requirement | edi-mcp |
| --- | --- |
| No `initialize` handshake, no sessions | Streamable HTTP runs with `stateless_http=True`: no `Mcp-Session-Id`, any instance answers any request. stdio also accepts the legacy handshake. |
| `server/discover` | Answered by the SDK with the supported versions, capabilities (tools, resources) and the server instructions. |
| Per-request `_meta` envelope | `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities` decides whether a tool may ask a follow-up question (MRTR elicitation). |
| Cacheable results | `tools/list` 5 min, `resources/list` and `resources/templates/list` 1 h, `server/discover` 5 min, `resources/read` 24 h for static guides and 1 h for derived content; `cacheScope` is always `public` because nothing depends on the caller. |
| `resultType` | `complete` on every result; `input_required` only for an MRTR follow-up. |
| `structuredContent` and `outputSchema` | Every tool declares an `outputSchema`; results carry `structuredContent` and the same JSON as text. Failures set `isError` with `structuredContent.error` (see [error codes](../tools/utilities.md#error-codes)). |
| JSON Schema 2020-12 | Every `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` declares the dialect. Pydantic's generated `title` keys are dropped from both, and descriptions from output schemas (the [tool reference](../tools/reference.md) keeps them). |
| Tool annotations | All four hints (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`) and a title on every tool. |
| Tool `_meta` | `io.edi-mcp/surface`, `io.edi-mcp/requiresKey`, `io.edi-mcp/endpoints`, and `io.edi-mcp/stdioOnly` on stdio-only tools. |
| Result `_meta` | The SDK's `io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo` plus `io.edi-mcp/upstream`: upstream request count, cache hits, the backend used and how the call authenticated (never the credential). |
| Deterministic `tools/list` | Sorted by name and fixed per deployment (transport and whether downloads are enabled); its serialized size has a conformance bound. |
| Header routing | `Mcp-Method` / `Mcp-Name` must match the body; protocol-version mismatches are `-32020` and unsupported versions `-32022` (see [Transports](transports.md)). |

## MRTR and requestState

The server supports multi round-trip requests: a tool can return an
`InputRequiredResult` with an elicitation form, and the client resumes by calling the
tool again with `inputResponses` and the `requestState` continuation. The
continuation is compact base64url JSON of at most 16 KiB, never contains a key, token
or authorization decision, and is rejected when malformed, issued for another tool, or
older than an hour. Elicitation is used only when the client declares support. No
released tool asks a question yet; the mechanism is covered by the conformance tests.

## Deliberately left out

edi-mcp uses none of the features the 2026-07-28 revision deprecates or that a
stateless server cannot honour: no legacy SSE transport, no sessions, no
`roots/list`, no `sampling/createMessage` and no `logging/setLevel`. A CI job greps
the source for them and fails if any appear.

## Measured size

With the eight tools registered today, `tools/list` is about 37 KB of compact JSON on
both transports. The conformance bound is 60,000 bytes and will be re-measured once
every planned tool has landed.

## Conformance tests

`tests/test_spec_conformance_2026_07_28.py` and `tests/transport/` run as their own
CI job: schema dialect and validity, annotations and `_meta`, sorted and stable
`tools/list` within its size bound, aliases accepted and unknown arguments rejected,
cache hints on lists and reads, `server/discover`, stateless requests in both eras,
result `_meta`, header routing, protocol-version errors, host allow-lists, resources
over HTTP, an MRTR round trip with a tampered continuation, a stateless session
manager, and a real stdio subprocess speaking both protocol eras.

[^mcp-spec]: Model Context Protocol specification, 2026-07-28. <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28>
[^python-sdk]: MCP Python SDK. <https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk>

# Transports

## stdio (default)

`edi-mcp` (or `edi-mcp --transport stdio`) serves one client over standard input and
output, the usual setup for Claude Code, Claude Desktop and other local clients. Only
MCP framing goes to stdout; logs go to stderr. The key in the server's environment
(`EDI_API_KEY`) is used for every call, and the stdio-only download tools, once
released, are offered only here. The SDK's stdio loop serves both protocol eras: a
client that starts with the legacy `initialize` handshake and a 2026-07-28 client
both work.

## Streamable HTTP (stateless)

`edi-mcp --transport http` serves on `127.0.0.1:8080` by default (`--bind-address`,
`--bind-port`)[^mcp-transports]:

| Route | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /mcp` (and `/mcp/`) | JSON-RPC over Streamable HTTP; one response per request (a single SSE frame, or JSON with `server.json_response`). |
| `GET /mcp`, `DELETE /mcp` | 405 with `Allow: POST`: the server sends no server-initiated messages and keeps no sessions. |
| `GET /healthz` | Liveness, always 200 while the process serves: `{"status": "ok", "version", "protocolVersion", "transport"}`. |
| `GET /readyz` | Readiness: 503 `{"status": "warming"}` during startup work, then 200 `{"status": "ready", "degraded", "keyConfigured"}`. It never reveals the key. |

The server runs stateless: there is no `Mcp-Session-Id`, and any instance can answer
any request, so it scales horizontally behind a load balancer. Every response carries
`X-Request-Id` (yours, if you sent a well-formed one). Request bodies are capped at
1 MiB (`server.max_request_body_size`).

### Header checks

For 2026-07-28 requests the SDK checks the HTTP headers against the JSON-RPC body:

* `Mcp-Method` must match the body's `method`, and `Mcp-Name` the tool name,
  resource URI or prompt name; a mismatch is HTTP 400.
* `MCP-Protocol-Version` must agree with the version in the request's `_meta`
  envelope (`-32020` otherwise); an unsupported version is `-32022`, with the
  supported versions in `error.data.supported`.

A request whose `MCP-Protocol-Version` header names an older revision is served in
the legacy era, still without a session.

### Host and origin checks

DNS-rebinding protection is on automatically for loopback binds. For a public
deployment set `server.public_base_url` (its host and origin join the allow-lists)
and optionally `server.allowed_hosts` / `server.allowed_origins`; a request with any
other `Host` gets 421. Behind a proxy that rewrites `Host`, set
`server.dns_rebinding_protection = false`.

### Per-request EDI API keys

Each HTTP caller sends its own EDI API key in the `X-EDI-Key` header (configurable
with `server.request_key_header`; turn it off with `server.accept_header_key =
false`). The header is honoured only when `server.public_base_url` starts with
`https://`, meaning TLS terminates in front of the server, or when
`server.allow_insecure_header_key` is set for development. Otherwise the header is
stripped before any handler sees it and one warning is logged.

A caller without a key is served from DataONE: the operator's configured key is not
lent to HTTP callers unless `server.share_config_key_over_http` is set, which is meant
for private deployments only. The MCP-level `Authorization` header is never forwarded
to EDI. Download tools are never offered over HTTP.

[^mcp-transports]: MCP specification — Transports. <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports>
