# Hosted HTTP deployment

A hosted edi-mcp lets many users connect with
`claude mcp add --transport http edi https://edi-mcp.example.org/mcp`. The HTTP
transport is stateless Streamable HTTP[^mcp-transports] at `/mcp`: no session
header, no server-initiated stream, so any instance can answer any request and
instances can sit behind a plain load balancer.

```bash
edi-mcp --transport http --bind-address 127.0.0.1 --bind-port 8080
```

`POST /mcp` takes JSON-RPC requests; `GET` and `DELETE` on `/mcp` return 405
with `Allow: POST`. `/mcp/` is served directly rather than redirected. Every
response carries an `x-request-id` header (the caller's own value when it is a
short safe token, otherwise a generated one) that also appears in the JSON logs.

## Configuration essentials

```bash
EDI_MCP_SERVER__TRANSPORT=http
EDI_MCP_SERVER__BIND_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1          # the proxy connects locally
EDI_MCP_SERVER__BIND_PORT=8080
EDI_MCP_SERVER__PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://edi-mcp.example.org
```

`public_base_url` does two things:

* its host and origin join the `Host` and `Origin` allow-lists
  (`server.allowed_hosts`, `server.allowed_origins`) used for DNS-rebinding
  protection. Add any other names the service answers on to those lists;
  `server.dns_rebinding_protection` forces the check on or off (unset leaves
  the SDK default, which is on for loopback binds or when allow-lists are set);
* when it starts with `https://`, it opens the TLS gate for per-caller keys
  (below).

Other HTTP settings: `server.json_response` answers `POST /mcp` with
`application/json` instead of a single SSE frame, and
`server.max_request_body_size` (default 1 MiB) caps request bodies. All settings
are listed on the [Configuration](../getting-started/configuration.md) page.

## EDI API keys over HTTP

Each caller brings their own EDI API key in the `X-EDI-Key` header (the name is
`server.request_key_header`). The header is honoured only when
`public_base_url` is `https://`; otherwise the middleware strips it before any
handler sees it and logs one warning. `server.allow_insecure_header_key`
overrides the gate for local development only.

A call with a key is served by PASTA; a call without one is served anonymously
from DataONE, as on stdio (see [Backends](../tools/backends.md)). The
operator's own key (`EDI_API_KEY` in the server's environment) is **not** lent
to HTTP callers unless `server.share_config_key_over_http` is true; enable that
only on a private deployment where every caller may act as the operator. The
MCP-level `Authorization` header is never forwarded to EDI. See
[Security](security.md) for the full key-handling rules.

## Behind a reverse proxy

Terminate TLS at the proxy (the key is a bearer secret), forward `Host`
unchanged, and pass `X-EDI-Key` through. uvicorn runs with proxy headers
enabled[^uvicorn]. Caddy[^caddy]:

```text
edi-mcp.example.org {
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8080
}
```

nginx:

```nginx
location / {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_buffering off;          # single SSE frame per response
}
```

## systemd

```ini
[Unit]
Description=edi-mcp (Streamable HTTP)
After=network-online.target

[Service]
User=edi
EnvironmentFile=/etc/edi-mcp.env
ExecStart=/opt/edi-mcp/.venv/bin/edi-mcp --transport http
Restart=on-failure
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=strict

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Keep `/etc/edi-mcp.env` readable by the service user only if it holds an
operator key.

## Container image

A `Dockerfile` (Python slim base, non-root user, health check on `/healthz`) is
planned for the v0.1.0 release and is not in the repository yet. Until then,
install the package into a virtual environment as above.

## Health and readiness

* `GET /healthz` is liveness only: always 200 with `status`, `version`,
  `protocolVersion` and `transport`; it contacts nothing upstream.
* `GET /readyz` returns 503 with `status: warming` while startup work runs, then
  200 with `status: ready`, `degraded` and `keyConfigured` (whether an operator
  key is set; the key itself is never shown).

## Not available over HTTP

Downloads exist only on stdio, confined to `downloads.directory`: the
download tools (planned for build step 6) are never listed over HTTP. Each instance keeps its own
in-memory response cache (`cache.*` settings), so instances do not share state.

[^mcp-transports]: MCP 2026-07-28 — Transports. <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports>
[^uvicorn]: Uvicorn — Deployment. <https://www.uvicorn.org/deployment/>
[^caddy]: Caddy — reverse_proxy. <https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy>

# Security

Since 2026-07-30 every PASTA endpoint needs credentials[^edi-news], so an EDI
API key is a real secret: it reads everything its owner can read, including
access-restricted packages. edi-mcp treats it accordingly. Version 1 is
**read-only**: no tool creates, updates or deletes anything in EDI, and the
only local writes will be the stdio-only downloads, confined to
`downloads.directory`.

## Where the key comes from

* **stdio:** the server's environment only. `EDI_API_KEY` (the name EDI's
  guides use[^edi-keys]) or `EDI_MCP_EDI__API_KEY`, which overrides it. There
  is no command-line flag (command lines leak into `ps` and shell history),
  `.env` files are not loaded automatically, and look-alike names
  (`EDI_KEY`, `EDI_TOKEN`, `EDI_AUTH_TOKEN`) are not read: the loader warns
  when one is set without `EDI_API_KEY`. A YAML `edi.api_key` also works but
  should not be committed.
* **HTTP:** each caller's `X-EDI-Key` header, honoured only when
  `server.public_base_url` is `https://` (or the development override
  `allow_insecure_header_key` is on); otherwise the header is stripped before
  any handler runs. The operator's key is not lent to callers unless
  `share_config_key_over_http` is enabled. The MCP-level `Authorization`
  header is never read for EDI and never forwarded upstream[^mcp-security].
  See [Hosted HTTP deployment](hosted-http.md).

A bad key is an error (`upstream_forbidden`), never a silent downgrade to
DataONE.

## What happens to the key

* The key is held in an `ApiKey` object whose `repr` and `str` never show it,
  and every key and token the process sees is registered with the log
  redactor.
* The key is exchanged for a short-lived `edi-token` (8 hours) at
  `auth.edirepository.org`. Tokens live in memory only, one slot per key
  identity (a truncated SHA-256 of the key), so HTTP callers with different
  keys never share a token. A token is refreshed once fewer than
  `edi.token_refresh_margin_s` seconds remain (default one hour); a 401 to a
  token triggers one re-exchange.
* The token is sent to PASTA as a hand-set `Cookie: edi-token=…` header. If
  the auth service is unreachable or failing, the key itself is sent as a
  `?key=` query parameter for `edi.auth_fallback_s` seconds (default 300). If
  the auth service rejects the key, the call fails.
* Credentials are attached **only** to requests for the PASTA host. DataONE,
  the member nodes and the citation service are always called anonymously.
* The HTTP client's cookie jar accepts no cookies, so the `edi-token` cookie
  PASTA sets (even on anonymous 403 responses) is never stored or replayed to
  another caller.
* Cached PASTA responses are keyed by the key's identity, so one caller's
  cached results are never served to another caller.

## What never leaves the server

* `scrub_url()` removes the `key` query parameter and redacts every
  registered secret from each URL that is surfaced: result `source` fields,
  `_meta` upstream labels, log lines, cache keys and error details. Endpoint
  labels (`GET host/path`) carry no query string at all.
* HTTP transport errors are re-raised without the underlying exception, whose
  message could contain a keyed URL.
* Logs go to stderr (stdout is MCP framing on stdio). A structlog processor
  masks values of credential-like keys (`token`, `authorization`, `api_key`,
  `x-edi-key`, `cookie`, …) and replaces registered secrets anywhere in a
  logged string.
* Upstream error text is cleaned before it reaches a result: registered
  secrets are redacted, EDI principals (`EDI-<40 hex>`) become `EDI-…`, and
  PASTA's 403 wording `User '…' is not authorized`, which names the caller,
  has the name removed.
* MRTR continuations (`requestState`) refuse credential-like keys and are
  capped at 16 KiB.

## Outbound requests

* Upstream hosts come from the `edi.*` URL settings: PASTA, the EDI auth
  service, the DataONE coordinating node, the two GMN member nodes and the
  citation service. Redirects are followed by hand, at most three, and only to
  `https://` hosts on that allow-list; anything else fails with an error.
* Response bodies are read with a byte cap (`edi.max_response_bytes`, default
  20 MiB), and EML documents larger than `limits.max_eml_bytes` are refused.
  Tool results are trimmed to `limits.max_result_bytes` and fail above
  `limits.hard_max_result_bytes`.
* Concurrency is bounded (`edi.max_concurrency`); 429 responses honour
  `Retry-After`, and 5xx and network errors are retried with backoff.

## Untrusted XML

EML metadata and DataONE Solr responses are parsed with `defusedxml`[^defusedxml]
only, which rejects entity expansion and external DTDs. Raw EML is not placed in
tool results.

## Test fixtures

Hermetic tests replay recorded responses, so fixtures must never carry a
secret. `scripts/record_fixtures.py record` never records auth-service traffic,
keeps no response headers except `Content-Type` and `Location`, and scrubs every
body before writing it: the key, every `edi-token` seen, anything JWT-shaped,
and the identity claims decoded from the token. Recordings replace the committed
set only if `check` passes; CI runs `check` on every push (no JWT-shaped string,
no `edi-token=`, no `set-cookie`, no `key=` in a manifest URL). The test router
fails a test if a credential reaches any host other than PASTA. See
[Testing](../develop/testing.md).

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report a suspected vulnerability privately to the
[idss-mesa](https://github.com/idss-mesa){target=_blank} maintainers rather than
in a public issue, and never paste a key or token into an issue, log or
fixture.

[^edi-news]: EDI news: authentication required for PASTA (2026-07-27). <https://edirepository.org/news/news-20260727.00>
[^edi-keys]: EDI — Working with access keys. <https://edirepository.org/resources/working-with-access-keys>
[^mcp-security]: MCP 2026-07-28 — Security best practices. <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/security_best_practices>
[^defusedxml]: defusedxml. <https://github.com/tiran/defusedxml>

# Adding a tool

[`edi_list_scopes`](../tools/reference.md#edi_list_scopes) in
`src/edi_mcp/tools/discovery.py` is a small real example; this is its shape.

## 1. Models

```python
class ListScopesIn(EdiInput):             # snake_case fields; extras rejected
    kind: ScopeKind | None = Field(
        None, description="Only one kind: lter (LTER sites), edi (general EDI submissions), ..."
    )


class ListScopesResult(ToolResultBase):   # envelope: resolved, notes, nextSteps, source
    budget_list: ClassVar[str | None] = "scopes"

    scopes: list[ScopeInfo]
    page: Page
    live: bool = Field(description="True when PASTA listed the scopes just now; ...")
    snapshot_as_of: str = Field(description="Date of the snapshot ...")   # dumped as snapshotAsOf
```

Inputs subclass `EdiInput` and use snake_case; outputs subclass
`ToolResultBase` and are dumped in camelCase with `None` omitted. Every input
field needs a `description`: it is what the model reads. A result with a long
list declares `budget_list` so the registry can trim it to the size budget
(see [Architecture](architecture.md#result-budget)).

## 2. Register the handler

```python
@register_tool(
    "edi_list_scopes",
    title="List EDI scopes",
    description=(
        "List the repository's scopes (knb-lter-hbr, edi, ...) with name, kind, ... "
        "Next: call edi_search_packages(scope=...) or edi_list_identifiers(scope=...)."
    ),
    input_model=ListScopesIn,
    output_model=ListScopesResult,
    surface="discovery",
    endpoints=["GET pasta.lternet.edu/package/eml"],
)
async def edi_list_scopes(args: ListScopesIn, ctx: ToolContext) -> ListScopesResult:
    backend = backend_for(ctx)
    if isinstance(backend, PastaBackend):
        names = await backend.list_scopes()
    else:
        ...   # DataONE has no scope listing: use the dated snapshot and say so in notes
```

The registry checks each declaration at import time:

* the name matches `^edi_[a-z_]+$`;
* the description is at most 600 characters and ends with a sentence starting
  `Next:`;
* the input model subclasses `EdiInput` and the output model `ToolResultBase`;
* `surface` is a known family.

Also:

* keep the annotations honest (`read_only`, `destructive`, `idempotent`,
  `open_world`);
* list every upstream endpoint the handler can call, on both backends;
* set `requires_key=True` for PASTA-only tools, so the registry fails fast with
  `auth_required` when the call has no key;
* restrict stdio-only tools with `transports=("stdio",)`.

Handlers call `backend_for(ctx)` and `resolve_scope` / `resolve_reference` /
`resolve_package`, never the HTTP client directly. Build `source` with
`tools._common.source(ctx)`, and fill `notes` (backend caveats, what was
assumed) and `nextSteps` (concrete follow-up calls). Finally, import the module
in `tools/__init__.py`.

## 3. Fixtures and tests

* Add the tool's real calls to `TOOL_SCENARIOS` in
  `scripts/record_fixtures.py` (on both backends where the tool supports both)
  and re-record. Fixtures come only from the recorder; see
  [Testing](testing.md).
* Test through `tests.helpers.call_ok`, which asserts success and validates the
  payload against the tool's `outputSchema`, and `call_err` for error codes.
  Cover the happy path on both backends, each filter, paging, error mapping
  and, for key-only tools, the `auth_required` fail-fast.
* Update the `KEY_TOOLS` and `WRITE_TOOLS` sets in
  `tests/test_spec_conformance_2026_07_28.py`, which check the
  `readOnlyHint` and requires-key metadata of every tool.

## 4. Regenerate the docs

```bash
uv run python scripts/gen_tools_reference.py   # docs/tools/reference.md
uv run python scripts/gen_llms_txt.py          # docs/llms.txt, docs/llms-full.txt
```

Describe the tool on its family page under `docs/tools/` and add a dated entry
to `docs/log.md`. The docs workflow fails when a generated file has drifted
from its sources.

    title: "neon-mcp (the sibling server edi-mcp's core is ported from)"
    author: "team:idss-mesa"
status: stable
---

# Architecture

edi-mcp copies the architecture of its sibling
[neon-mcp](https://github.com/idss-mesa/neon-mcp){target=_blank}: one SDK-coupled
adapter, an SDK-independent tool registry, handlers that return pydantic models,
and one upstream HTTP client. What is new is the backend layer: every tool call
is served by PASTA when it has an EDI API key and by DataONE when it does not.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  client[MCP client] -->|stdio / Streamable HTTP| transport[transport/]
  transport --> adapter[server.py\nEdiServer]
  adapter --> registry[registry.py\nvalidate · auth · budget]
  registry --> ctx[context.py\nkey → backend]
  registry --> tools[tools/*]
  tools --> scopes[edi/scopes.py\nedi/pid.py]
  tools --> backends[edi/backends/\nPasta · DataOne]
  backends --> client2[edi/client.py]
  client2 --> tokens[edi/tokens.py]
  client2 --> cache[edi/cache.py]
  client2 -->|edi-token cookie| pasta[(PASTA)]
  client2 -->|anonymous| d1[(DataONE CN + GMN)]
  client2 -->|anonymous| cite[(cite.edirepository.org)]
```

## Request flow

1. **Transport.** stdio, or stateless Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, where a raw ASGI
   middleware assigns a request id and exposes the request headers (with
   `X-EDI-Key` removed unless the TLS gate allows it) through context variables.
2. **Adapter.** `server.py` is the only module that imports the MCP SDK. It
   serves `tools/list` (sorted, JSON Schema 2020-12, cache hints) and turns a
   `tools/call` into a registry invocation, returning compact JSON text,
   `structuredContent` and `io.edi-mcp/*` `_meta`.
3. **Context.** `build_tool_context` resolves the call's key (`resolve_key` in
   `edi/auth.py`: the configured key on stdio; the caller's header key, or the
   operator key when sharing is enabled, over HTTP). `ctx.backend` is `pasta`
   with a key and `dataone` without.
4. **Registry.** `invoke` validates the arguments against the tool's input
   model, fails fast with `auth_required` for `requires_key` tools when there is
   no key, runs the handler, dumps the output model (camelCase, `None`
   omitted), stamps a default `source`, and enforces the result budget.
5. **Tool.** A handler is `async (args, ctx) -> OutputModel`. It resolves scopes
   and package references (`resolve_scope`, `resolve_reference`, or
   `resolve_package`) and calls `backend_for(ctx)`; it never calls the HTTP
   client directly.
6. **Backend.** `PastaBackend` and `DataOneBackend` implement one contract and
   return the same plain dataclasses, so tools do not branch on the backend.
   Each records its upstream calls in the call's `UpstreamStats` and adds its
   caveats to `notes`.
7. **Client.** `EdiClient` attaches credentials to PASTA requests only, retries,
   follows allow-listed redirects by hand, caps body sizes and caches responses.

## Result budget

Every tool result is measured as compact JSON. Above
`limits.max_result_bytes` (default 50 000), `fit_to_budget` trims the output
model's declared `budget_list` (eliding URL-like fields first, when the model
names them), marks the page `truncated` with `truncatedReason: budget` and a
`nextOffset`, and adds a note. A result still above
`limits.hard_max_result_bytes` (default 200 000) fails with `result_too_large`.

## Module map

| Module | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `__main__.py` | CLI: flags → config → logging → serve; `--check` (offline config check and in-process `edi_ping`), `--print-config` (key redacted) |
| `config.py` | pydantic settings; flag > `EDI_MCP_*` env > YAML > defaults; the key from `EDI_API_KEY` or `EDI_MCP_EDI__API_KEY` |
| `server.py` | the SDK adapter: tools, resources, cache hints, MRTR, upstream `_meta` |
| `registry.py` | `@register_tool` and its checks, argument validation, fail-fast `auth_required`, `fit_to_budget`, the `requestState` codec |
| `context.py` | `ToolContext` (config, key, backend, stats); request-scoped context variables |
| `errors.py` | `ToolError` codes and the upstream error mapping (`upstream_forbidden`, `access_restricted`, …) |
| `logging.py` | structlog to stderr; credential masking and registered-secret redaction |
| `instructions.py` | server instructions returned by `server/discover` |
| `resources.py`, `resources_static/` | `edi://` guides (`api-key`, `package-identifiers`) and the dated scope snapshot `scopes.json` |
| `models/common.py` | `EdiInput`, `ToolResultBase`, `Page`, `Resolved`, `Source` |
| `edi/auth.py` | `ApiKey`, per-call key resolution, the HTTP TLS gate, `scrub_url` |
| `edi/tokens.py` | key → `edi-token` exchange and refresh per key identity, `?key=` fallback |
| `edi/client.py` | the one `httpx` client: PASTA-only credentials, cookie jar that stores nothing, retries, allow-listed redirects, byte caps, upstream error scrubbing |
| `edi/cache.py` | per-family TTL cache with single-flight and stale-if-error; PASTA entries keyed by key identity |
| `edi/backends/` | the `Backend` contract, `PastaBackend`, `DataOneBackend`, `backend_for`, `resolve_package` |
| `edi/pid.py` | package identifier, DOI and URL parsing |
| `edi/scopes.py` | scope snapshot, scope names, LTER site codes and `name.identifier` references |
| `edi/xml.py`, `edi/eml.py` | defusedxml parsing and EML prose; EML data-entity references and sizes |
| `projections/eml.py` | parsed EML → compact, capped models (people, coverage, methods, license, project, entities and attributes), with `<references>` resolution |
| `tools/` | one module per family (`core.py`, `discovery.py`, `packages.py`, which fetches and parses the EML once per call via `load()`), plus helpers in `_common.py` (`source`, `paginate`, `portal_url`) |
| `transport/` | stdio; stateless Streamable HTTP with `/healthz`, `/readyz` and the request-context middleware |

Preview, download, citation and the key-only tools arrive in build step 6 (see the
[Roadmap](../tools/roadmap.md)).

Design decisions and their reasons are recorded in `DESIGN.md` (the D-numbers)
and verified API facts in `RESEARCH.md`, both at the repository root.

# Contributing

1. Branch from `main` and open a pull request. One change per pull request;
   CI must be green before it is merged.
2. Before pushing, run the same checks CI runs:

    ```bash
    uv run ruff check src tests scripts && uv run ruff format --check src tests scripts
    uv run mypy --strict src
    uv run pytest
    uv run python scripts/record_fixtures.py check
    ```

    If the change touches upstream behaviour, also run the live tests with a key
    (see [Testing](testing.md)).
3. Never commit `.env`, a key, an `edi-token`, or a fixture that did not come
   from `scripts/record_fixtures.py record`.

## Design and research records

* `DESIGN.md` keeps the decision register. Each decision has a D-number (D1
  hybrid backend, D2 bad keys, D4 credential form, D9 identifiers, …) with the
  question, the decision and the reason. Changing behaviour that a decision
  covers means updating that row in the same pull request; code comments cite
  the D-number.
* `RESEARCH.md` records verified EDI, DataONE and MCP facts with the date each
  was checked. PASTA and DataONE change without notice, so a new upstream fact
  goes in with its date, and a fact that stopped being true is corrected rather
  than deleted silently.
* `CLAUDE.md` and the code map summarise both for coding agents; keep them in
  step.

## Two change logs

* `CHANGELOG.md` (repository root) is the package release log, in the Keep a
  Changelog format[^keepachangelog]. Add user-visible changes under
  `[Unreleased]`.
* `docs/log.md` is the documentation bundle's log. Every docs change adds a
  dated `## YYYY-MM-DD` entry naming the pages created or updated.

## Documentation

The `docs/` tree is an Open Knowledge Format (OKF v0.2)[^okf-spec] bundle built
with Zensical. Content pages carry YAML frontmatter (`title`, `description`,
`type`, `tags`, `generated`, `sources`, `status`); section `index.md` files carry
none. After changing docs or tools:

```bash
uv run python scripts/gen_tools_reference.py    # when a tool changed
uv run python scripts/gen_config_reference.py   # when a setting changed
uv run python scripts/gen_llms_txt.py           # always: docs/llms.txt, docs/llms-full.txt
uv run python scripts/okf_validate.py docs
uv run zensical build --clean --strict
```

Commit the generated files; the docs workflow fails when they drift from their
sources. Pages may only state what the code on `main` does; tools that are not
merged yet belong on the [Roadmap](../tools/roadmap.md).

## Versioning

edi-mcp follows Semantic Versioning[^semver]. The version lives in
`src/edi_mcp/__init__.py`. The first release, v0.1.0, and its release workflow
are planned for build step 7.

[^keepachangelog]: Keep a Changelog 1.1.0. <https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/>
[^semver]: Semantic Versioning. <https://semver.org/>
[^okf-spec]: Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.2 specification. <https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md>

# Testing

```bash
uv sync --all-extras
uv run pytest                                   # hermetic unit + conformance tests
uv run ruff check src tests scripts && uv run ruff format --check src tests scripts
uv run mypy --strict src
uv run python scripts/record_fixtures.py check  # fixtures carry no secrets
```

## Hermetic tests

`uv run pytest` makes no network calls: live tests are deselected by default
(`-m 'not live'`). Every upstream request goes through
`tests/fixture_router.py`, a stand-in for PASTA, the EDI auth service, DataONE
and the citation service, driven by `tests/fixtures/manifest.json`. The router:

* answers the auth service itself with fake JWTs for a test key, so no real
  token is ever stored;
* enforces PASTA's credential rules: no credential gets the recorded anonymous
  403, an unknown token or a wrong `?key=` gets 401;
* fails the test when a credential (cookie or `key`) reaches any host other
  than PASTA;
* records every request in `FixtureRouter.calls`, and fails the test on any
  request it has no fixture for.

Tool tests go through `tests.helpers.call_ok`, which asserts success and
validates the payload against the tool's `outputSchema`, and `call_err`, which
asserts an error code. The suite also covers the registry, config precedence,
log redaction, error mapping, the identifier parser (with hypothesis), the
cache, both backends, the transports (stdio in both protocol eras, Streamable
HTTP, `X-EDI-Key` passthrough, health endpoints) and MCP 2026-07-28
conformance (`tests/test_spec_conformance_2026_07_28.py`).

The coverage gate is 85% (`fail_under` in `pyproject.toml`, branch coverage):

```bash
uv run pytest --cov=edi_mcp --cov-report=term
```

## Recording fixtures

Fixtures come only from `scripts/record_fixtures.py`, never from hand edits.
`record` drives the real backends (PASTA with `EDI_API_KEY`, DataONE without)
and the scenarios in `TOOL_SCENARIOS` (real tool calls on both backends)
through a recording transport, so fixtures match the exact requests edi-mcp
makes:

```bash
set -a; . ./.env; set +a          # loads EDI_API_KEY without printing it
uv run python scripts/record_fixtures.py record
```

It never records auth-service traffic, stores no response headers except
`Content-Type` and `Location`, and scrubs every body before writing it: the
key, every `edi-token` it saw, anything JWT-shaped, and the identity claims
decoded from the token. Recordings land in the gitignored `tests/fixtures/_raw/`
and replace the committed set only if `check` passes on them.

`check` (run in CI on every push) fails on a JWT-shaped string, `edi-token=`,
`set-cookie`, `key=` in a manifest URL, the API key itself when `EDI_API_KEY` is
set, a missing manifest file, a fixture over 40 KB, or a total over 3 MB.

## Live tests

Live tests hit the real services and are opt-in. DataONE tests run anonymously;
PASTA tests also need `EDI_API_KEY` and skip without it.

```bash
set -a; . ./.env; set +a
EDI_MCP_LIVE=1 uv run pytest -m live tests/live
```

They assert behaviour that fixtures cannot: that sorted searches come back in
order (PASTA silently ignores a malformed sort, so an HTTP 200 proves nothing),
that bounding-box, author and temporal filters return the right region and
records, and that the dated scope snapshot is current (a known scope leaving
PASTA fails; new scopes only warn). DataONE's index changes without notice
(see `RESEARCH.md`), so a failing live test can mean upstream drift rather than
a regression.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on pushes to `main`, pull requests, manual
dispatch and nightly:

* **test** on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13: ruff check and format, `mypy
  --strict`, the fixture `check`, and the full suite with coverage;
* **test (macOS)**: smoke and stdio transport tests on Python 3.12;
* **MCP 2026-07-28 conformance**: asserts the SDK is `mcp` 2.x, runs the
  conformance and transport tests, and fails on deprecated MCP features in
  `src/` (sampling, roots, `logging/setLevel`, the legacy SSE transport,
  session ids);
* **live smoke (nightly)**: on schedule and manual dispatch, with
  `EDI_MCP_LIVE=1` and the repository secret `EDI_API_KEY` (PASTA tests skip
  when the secret is not set).

## Documentation checks

`.github/workflows/docs.yml` validates the docs on every pull request and
deploys the site from `main`:

```bash
uv run python scripts/okf_validate.py docs      # OKF v0.2 frontmatter and reserved files
uv run python scripts/gen_llms_txt.py           # docs/llms.txt, docs/llms-full.txt
uv run python scripts/gen_tools_reference.py    # docs/tools/reference.md
uv run python scripts/gen_config_reference.py   # settings table in configuration.md
git diff --exit-code docs/                      # CI fails if a generated file drifted
uv run zensical build --clean --strict          # broken links fail the build
```

# For AI agents

This site is published for people **and** for AI agents. The documentation
source is an [Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.2](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md){target=_blank}
knowledge bundle[^okf-spec], and the deployed site exposes that structure
directly. If you are an agent (or you are wiring one up), consume the
documentation through the endpoints below rather than scraping rendered HTML.

## This site documents an MCP server

edi-mcp *is* an agent tool. If what you actually want is EDI data —
packages, scopes, revisions, metadata — do not scrape these pages: connect to
the server and call its tools. Locally, run it over `stdio`
(`claude mcp add edi -s user -- edi-mcp --transport stdio`); against a
hosted instance, use Streamable HTTP at `https://<host>/mcp`
(`claude mcp add --transport http edi https://<host>/mcp`). The server
implements MCP 2026-07-28[^mcp-spec]: `server/discover` and `tools/list`
return the live, authoritative tool catalogue with JSON Schema inputs and
outputs, and every list result carries cache hints. Use this documentation
to learn *how* to use the server; use the server to get the data.

## Entry points

All URLs are under `https://idss-mesa.github.io/edi-mcp/`.

| Endpoint | What you get |
| -------- | ------------ |
| [`llms.txt`](../llms.txt) — `https://idss-mesa.github.io/edi-mcp/llms.txt` | Linked outline of every page with one-line descriptions ([llms.txt convention](https://llmstxt.org){target=_blank}[^llmstxt]) |
| [`llms-full.txt`](../llms-full.txt) — `https://idss-mesa.github.io/edi-mcp/llms-full.txt` | The entire corpus in one file: every page's Markdown with frontmatter, each prefixed by its canonical URL |
| Any page URL + `index.md` | That page's Markdown source with full OKF frontmatter, e.g. `https://idss-mesa.github.io/edi-mcp/getting-started/api-key/index.md` |
| `https://idss-mesa.github.io/edi-mcp/sitemap.xml`, `https://idss-mesa.github.io/edi-mcp/robots.txt` | Standard crawl surface; `robots.txt` welcomes AI fetchers and repeats these pointers |
| [`tools/reference/`](../tools/reference.md) — `https://idss-mesa.github.io/edi-mcp/tools/reference/` | The tool catalogue generated from the server's registry: every tool's inputs, result fields, endpoints and key requirement |
| [Source repository](https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp){target=_blank} | The bundle itself under `docs/`, plus `CLAUDE.md` with the rules coding agents follow when editing the code |

Every rendered page also declares its Markdown twin and OKF signals in its
HTML `<head>`, as `okf:`-prefixed meta tags named after the frontmatter keys
(`type`, `status`, `trust-tier`, `generated-at`, `generated-by`,
`stale-after`) — for example:

```html
<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="index.md">
<meta name="okf:status" content="stable">
<meta name="okf:trust-tier" content="unverified">
<meta name="okf:generated-at" content="2026-10-19T00:00:00Z">
<meta name="okf:generated-by" content="claude/opus-5.5">
<meta name="okf:stale-after" content="2027-04-19T00:00:00Z">
```

The page's `type` is exposed the same way, so a crawler can filter by kind of
page (Guide, Reference, Policy, ...) without parsing frontmatter.

## Reading the OKF frontmatter

Each content page's YAML frontmatter answers the questions an agent should
ask before relying on it[^okf-spec]:

* **What is this?** — `type` (`Guide`, `Tutorial`, `Reference`, `Policy`,
  `MCP Tool Reference`), `title`, `description`, `tags`.
* **Where did it come from?** — `generated: { by, at }` records the actor
  that produced the current text and when it last changed meaningfully;
  `sources` lists the load-bearing external references (`id`, `resource`
  URL, `title`, `author`). Footnotes in the body cite sources by their `id`.
* **How much should I trust it?** — the `verified` key (see trust tiers
  below). Its absence is meaningful: the page has not been confirmed by
  anyone other than its generator.
* **Is it still true?** — `status` (`stable` is the default; `draft` needs
  review; `deprecated` is kept for history only) and `stale_after`, an
  ISO 8601 instant after which the page should be re-checked. Pages that
  state facts EDI, DataONE or the MCP project may change — key rules,
  endpoints, SDK versions — carry one.

Actors follow OKF §7: `<producer>/<version>` for agents and tools (for
example `claude/opus-5.5`), `human:<id>` for a person, `process:<id>` for an
automated job such as the generated tool reference.

## Trust tiers

| `verified` key | Tier | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| absent | **unverified** | Generated content nobody has confirmed against its sources. Most pages on this site start here. |
| present, non-`human:` actors only | **machine-confirmed** | An automated check (a CI job, a live smoke test) confirmed the content. |
| present with a `human:<id>` actor | **human-reviewed** | A maintainer read and confirmed the page. Prefer these when answers conflict. |

Only humans add `verified:` entries; a generator never does. The
`okf:trust-tier` meta tag carries the derived tier for quick filtering.

## Answering user questions

Ground answers in this documentation and cite the page URL (for example
`https://idss-mesa.github.io/edi-mcp/getting-started/api-key/`). For
anything about the *data* — package ids, scopes, revisions, DOIs, entity
names — call the server or the
[EDI repository](https://edirepository.org){target=_blank}
rather than guessing from prose. When the corpus does not answer a question
about edi-mcp itself, direct users to the
[GitHub issue tracker](https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp/issues){target=_blank}.

[^okf-spec]: Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.2 specification. <https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md>
[^llmstxt]: The /llms.txt convention. <https://llmstxt.org>
[^mcp-spec]: Model Context Protocol specification, 2026-07-28. <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28>

# Citing EDI data

edi-mcp is only a conduit. The data packages it finds belong to their creators and are
published by the Environmental Data Initiative (EDI). The intellectual rights stated in
each package, together with EDI's data policy[^edi-policy], govern how you may use and
credit them; this project's license does not.

## What to cite: one revision, one DOI

An EDI data package is identified as `scope.identifier.revision`, for example
`knb-lter-hbr.14.22` (scope `knb-lter-hbr`, the Hubbard Brook LTER; identifier `14`;
revision `22`). Published revisions are immutable: changes to a package appear as a new
revision, and each revision has its own DOI of the form `doi:10.6073/pasta/<md5>`.
Cite the revision you actually used, by its DOI, so that others get the same data.
[Package identifiers](../tools/identifiers.md) explains the formats edi-mcp accepts.

## Citation styles

EDI's citation service, `cite.edirepository.org`, formats a citation for any public
package without a key[^edi-cite]. It offers the ESIP, DRYAD and BIBTEX styles, and JSON
fields with `Accept: application/json`. For `knb-lter-hbr.14.22` on 2026-10-19:

=== "ESIP"

    > USDA Forest Service, Northern Research Station. 2026. Hubbard Brook Experimental
    > Forest: Total Daily Precipitation by Watershed, 1956 - ongoing ver 22.
    > Environmental Data Initiative.
    > https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/2017345f0977c0f7c46e1ad90ce1b062.

=== "DRYAD"

    > USDA Forest Service, Northern Research Station (2026) Hubbard Brook Experimental
    > Forest: Total Daily Precipitation by Watershed, 1956 - ongoing. Environmental Data
    > Initiative. https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/2017345f0977c0f7c46e1ad90ce1b062

=== "BIBTEX"

    ```bibtex
    @misc{knb-lter-hbr.14.22,
        author={USDA Forest Service, Northern Research Station},
        title={{Hubbard Brook Experimental Forest: Total Daily Precipitation by Watershed, 1956 - ongoing. ver 22}},
        year={2026},
        publisher={Environmental Data Initiative},
        doi={10.6073/pasta/2017345f0977c0f7c46e1ad90ce1b062},
        url={https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/2017345f0977c0f7c46e1ad90ce1b062},
        note = {Type: dataset}
    }
    ```

You can request these yourself, for example
`https://cite.edirepository.org/cite/knb-lter-hbr.14.22?style=ESIP`. The EDI Data
Portal's landing page for each package shows the same citation.

!!! note "edi_get_citation is planned"

    A dedicated `edi_get_citation` tool that returns these styles is part of the next
    build step and is not available yet (see the [Roadmap](../tools/roadmap.md)). Until
    then, `edi_search_packages` returns each package's `doi` and `portalUrl`, from which
    the citation above can be retrieved.

## Intellectual rights

EDI curates each package with the intellectual rights its provider declared in the EML
metadata. EDI advocates open access without use restrictions but allows providers to
declare more restrictive licenses. When a provider declares none, EDI adds a default
statement based on the Creative Commons CC0 1.0 "No Rights Reserved" waiver, which also
asks for attribution as professional etiquette[^edi-policy]. Check the rights stated in
the package you use rather than assuming a license; some packages are also
access-restricted and need permission from their contacts.

## About edi-mcp itself

If you retrieved data through edi-mcp you may mention the tool in your methods, but the
citation of record is always the data package DOI. Never cite PASTA or DataONE download
URLs. The edi-mcp server software is MIT-licensed by The Regents of the University of
New Mexico[^edi-mcp-license] and is not affiliated with or endorsed by EDI, the LTER
Network or DataONE. See [License](license.md).

[^edi-policy]: EDI Policy — Data policy, version 2.0 (updated 2026-04-01). <https://edirepository.org/about/edi-policy>
[^edi-cite]: EDI citation service. <https://cite.edirepository.org/cite/knb-lter-hbr.14.22?style=ESIP>
[^edi-mcp-license]: edi-mcp `LICENSE` file. <https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE>

# License

Three things meet on this site: the server software, the documentation you are
reading, and the EDI data packages the server gives access to. Each has its own license.

## Server code — MIT

The edi-mcp source code (the `edi_mcp` Python package, the `edi-mcp` command-line
program, tests and build scripts) is released under the
[MIT License](https://opensource.org/license/mit){target=_blank}[^mit]:

> Copyright (c) 2026 The Regents of the University of New Mexico

The full text is in the repository's
[`LICENSE`](https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE){target=_blank}
file[^edi-mcp-license]. In short: you may use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute,
sublicense and sell the software, provided the copyright notice and permission notice
are included; the software is provided "as is", without warranty.

## Documentation text — CC-BY 4.0

The prose, tables and examples on this site (everything under `docs/` in the
repository, including the OKF frontmatter) are licensed under
[Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/){target=_blank}[^cc-by-4].
You may share and adapt the material for any purpose, provided you give appropriate
credit ("edi-mcp documentation, idss-mesa / The Regents of the University of New
Mexico, CC-BY 4.0") and indicate whether changes were made. Code snippets embedded in
the documentation may alternatively be used under the MIT terms above.

## EDI data — per package

Data packages retrieved from EDI through edi-mcp are not part of this project and are
not covered by either license above. Each package states its own intellectual rights in
its EML metadata. EDI advocates open access but lets providers declare more restrictive
terms; when a provider declares none, EDI applies a default statement based on the
CC0 1.0 waiver[^edi-policy]. Read the rights of each package you use, and cite it as
described in [Citing EDI data](citing-edi.md).

## Trademarks and affiliation

edi-mcp is an independent project of
[idss-mesa](https://github.com/idss-mesa){target=_blank} at the University of New
Mexico. It is not developed, endorsed or supported by the Environmental Data
Initiative, the LTER Network, DataONE or the U.S. National Science Foundation. Their
names belong to their respective owners; this site uses its own original artwork.

[^mit]: The MIT License. <https://opensource.org/license/mit>
[^edi-mcp-license]: edi-mcp `LICENSE` file. <https://github.com/idss-mesa/edi-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE>
[^cc-by-4]: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International. <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/>
[^edi-policy]: EDI Policy — Data policy. <https://edirepository.org/about/edi-policy>

* **Creation**: [Packages, metadata and entities](tools/packages.md) — `edi_get_package`, `edi_get_metadata` and `edi_list_entities` (build step 5), now on `main`.
* **Update**: [Tool reference](tools/reference.md) regenerated (8 tools); [Discovery](tools/discovery.md) — DataONE date sorting by upload date and legacy identifiers replace the known-issue box; [Roadmap](tools/roadmap.md), [Quickstart](getting-started/quickstart.md), [EDI API key](getting-started/api-key.md), [Architecture](develop/architecture.md), [MCP 2026-07-28 conformance](mcp/spec-2026-07-28.md) and the home page updated for step 5.
